docs.title: From installation to inference
docs.text:
New to the project? Start with the Quickstart for the complete first-run route.

  1. Prepare your runtime. Follow the GPU or NPU guide and verify the installed package versions.
  2. Prepare the model and catalog. Use the same model and tokenizer snapshot when building the constraint artifact and running inference.
  3. Run Beam Search V1. Follow First offline inference to run one request and understand the returned SIDs.
  4. Serve requests over HTTP. Follow Online serving to start a GPU or NPU service and send an OpenAI-compatible Beam request.

See Beam parameters and modes before changing search widths, candidate counts, generation budgets, or graph settings.

docs.title: Advanced Beam workflows
docs.text:
Choose one advanced workflow after the first offline request works. These routes describe source snapshot c4966f18; their presence is not a claim of hardware validation for every model or combination. Keep models and capabilities and validation alongside the examples. Reuse the local model snapshot from Quickstart. Selecting a mode does not add SID tokens, trained recommendation weights, or thinking ability to a checkpoint.

Goal Change Keep separate Spend fewer or more rows at later stages Dynamic retained widths Engine capacity and final return limit Search without a business catalog Unconstrained Beam configuration Ordinary sampled text generation Emit A/B/C families without catalog membership NPU SID stage domain Full-vocabulary probability normalization Think before selecting SIDs The offline demo's combined --cot workflow Thinking budget and SID generation budget Limit each parent's candidates or choose catalog roots CUDA request/configuration extensions NPU capabilities in this snapshot

docs.title: Narrow or widen the active Beam
docs.text:
Use the dynamic-width examples for runnable NPU commands. Keep engine beam.max_width and request beam_width at 128; a schedule changes retained prefixes, not that capacity:

Retained widths after A/B/C Decode input widths Final return limit example [128, 64, 32] 128, 64 result_width=16 [32, 64, 128] 32, 64 result_width=16

The last retained width has no following model forward. NPU Beam graphs match exact (logical_batch_size, Decode_input_width) shapes. The demo derives its capture widths; a custom integration must configure them before engine startup. The maximum-capacity width is also captured. See NPU graph shapes for the capture-count limit and fallback behavior.

Leave scalar constraint_table.candidate_width unset for changing NPU widths. NPU's current path does not support independent candidate schedules. Python and HTTP expose dynamic retained widths on CUDA too, although the standalone demo's dynamic CLI flags are NPU-only. Narrowing prunes prefixes; later widening cannot recover them. Validate recommendation quality for the chosen search.

docs.title: Search the full vocabulary without a catalog
docs.text:
The catalog-based offline demo does not have an unconstrained Beam CLI flag. Use GRLLM.beam_search_v1() with an explicitly disabled table instead. This is Beam Search, not GRLLM.generate() sampling, and outputs need not be SIDs.

The following is a modification fragment, not a standalone program. Adapt the complete Python integration inside its main(): replace the entire block from config = load_gr_config(...) through the final candidate-capacity check with this configuration, then replace params. Keep the earlier backend/model checks, main guard, context manager, native engine settings, and compact-output handling. Recompute candidate_width as shown; the existing constructor uses it in max_logprobs=candidate_width. Use BACKEND=npu, ModelRunner V1, block_size=128, and enforce_eager=True for this initial case. Do not append this fragment after checks requiring an enabled catalog table.

from vllm_gr.config import gr_config_from_mapping, resolve_candidate_width

mode_config = {
    "schema_version": 1,
    "attention_backend": "CUSTOM",
    "constrained_generation": False,
    "beam": {
        "execution_mode": "v1",
        "worker_decision": True,
        "graph_enabled": False,
        "graph_batch_size": 1,
        "online_batch_sizes": [1],
        "max_width": 128,
        "max_decode_steps": 3,
    },
    "constraint_table": {
        "enabled": False,
        "backend": "npu",
        "max_top_k": 128,
    },
}
config = gr_config_from_mapping(mode_config)
candidate_width = resolve_candidate_width(config)
params = BeamSearchParams(
    beam_width=128, max_tokens=3, temperature=0.0, ignore_eos=True
)

No artifact path, artifact/tokenizer digest, or vocabulary slice is configured. The request omits BEGIN/END positions, so max_tokens=3 means three generated tokens, and no BEGIN is appended; update any integration log saying otherwise. Keep complete prompt tokenization and enforce its context budget.

The NPU adapter in this snapshot supports only one, two, or three generated tokens, ModelRunner V1, a supported plain text decoder in FP16/BF16, asynchronous scheduling, disabled Chunked Prefill, and TP/PP/DP/DCP/PCP=1. Existing Beam attention/KV dependencies remain required. The selector does not promise a performance gain over constrained TopK. See the complete unconstrained contract for configuration and finite-logit handling. Longer ordinary LLM generation does not extend this NPU Beam horizon.

docs.title: Restrict NPU token families without a catalog
docs.text:
SID stage mode is an optional specialization of the unconstrained configuration. Before constructing a new engine, change the preceding fragment as follows:

mode_config["beam"]["sid_stage_vocab"] = True
config = gr_config_from_mapping(mode_config)
candidate_width = resolve_candidate_width(config)
params = BeamSearchParams(
    beam_width=128,
    max_tokens=5,
    temperature=0.0,
    ignore_eos=True,
    begin_token="<|sid_begin|>",
    end_token="<|sid_end|>",
    include_stop_str_in_output=True,
)

After choosing either unconstrained variant's params, check its request boundary before constructing the engine. Retain the Python integration's nonempty-prompt and full-context-budget checks before the Beam call:

effective_steps = (
    params.max_tokens - int(params.begin_token is not None)
    - int(params.end_token is not None)
)
if params.beam_width != config.beam_max_width:
    raise ValueError("Request width must match the configured capacity")
if not 1 <= effective_steps <= min(3, config.beam_max_decode_steps):
    raise ValueError("Keep the NPU effective budget within 1..3 and engine capacity")

The SID-stage variant uses OneRec's markers and matching tokenizer. Supply the model's intended prompt; the API adds BEGIN, so do not add another copy yourself. Prefill selects A, followed by B and C in two Decode forwards. Token families come from the tokenizer's registered <s_a_N>, <s_b_N>, and <s_c_N> IDs. The stage domain is NPU-only, opt-in, and limited to three components.

Every combination within those families is eligible; there is no catalog membership check. Scores are normalized over the complete current SID family, not the full vocabulary or only the selected TopK candidates. Changing that domain can change scores and cross-parent rankings.

VLLM_GR_NPU_STAGE_LM_HEAD=0 disables the stage-projection optimization while preserving the same SID domain, providing a reference for that optimization. It does not restore full-vocabulary probabilities. Setting the variable to 1 alone does not enable SID stage mode. Set it before starting a fresh process; compare implementations under the same domain and inputs.

docs.title: Generate thinking text, or think before SID Beam
docs.text:
Both thinking modes require a compatible checkpoint and preserve the complete input. The combined mode also requires dedicated <think> and </think> tokens plus a matching SID catalog. A flag cannot add reasoning proficiency to untrained weights. Keep the NPU environment from the installation guide loaded.

The commands below reuse MODEL and CATALOG from Data and constraints, and create a separate full prompt. Keep the model's own intended question/history when replacing it:

export COT_DIR="$PWD/results/advanced-beam"
export THINK_PROMPT="$COT_DIR/prompt.txt"
mkdir -p "$COT_DIR"
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
cat > "$THINK_PROMPT" <<'EOF'
Video history: <|sid_begin|><s_a_346><s_b_6566><s_c_5603><|sid_end|>.
Consider this history and recommend the next video.
EOF

Choose one mode, not both:

Thinking onlyThinking then SID Beam 
python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" --prompt "$THINK_PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend npu --execution eager \
  --batch-size 1 --enable-thinking \
  --max-tokens 1024 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --temperature 0 --top-p 1 --top-k -1 \
  --output-json "$COT_DIR/thinking.json"

python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" --catalog "$CATALOG" --prompt "$THINK_PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend npu --execution eager \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 --generated-steps 3 \
  --cot --cot-max-tokens 1024 --cot-on-limit error --max-model-len 8192 \
  --temperature 0 --top-p 1 --top-k -1 --print-beams 5 \
  --output-json "$COT_DIR/cot-beam.json"

--enable-thinking uses ordinary generation with constraints disabled and no SID Beam phase. Its --max-tokens covers the complete continuation, including any thinking and final answer. --cot-max-tokens instead limits the combined mode's thinking phase; --generated-steps still controls SID components. The complete prompt, thinking allowance, separator, and SID boundaries must fit --max-model-len. Both modes ignore --input-len; do not truncate the question to make the thinking budget fit.

Plain text uses the checkpoint's chat template. Serialized Qwen ChatML needs real line breaks or one complete JSON string; bare ChatML with ambiguous literal \n is rejected. The parser preserves earlier messages and reopens only the supported terminal empty assistant/thinking prefix. Read the input and handoff contract before using serialized prompts.

The default combined policy requires a natural </think> before Beam starts. An unclosed span, including an early EOS, fails the batch. If you deliberately choose --cot-on-limit truncate, only a real length-budget exhaustion permits forced closure; every token is retained and the report marks truncation and forced closure. This is not a naturally completed thought. Other incomplete stop conditions still fail. Increase the budget or fix the model/prompt first.

Both phases use one loaded engine but hand off token IDs with separate cache salts and a fresh Beam Prefill; thinking KV is not reused across phases. This does not extend the three-level SID table. The source workflow documents NPU commands; CUDA hardware validation of the combined example is not included.

docs.title: CUDA per-parent candidates and multiple catalog roots
docs.text:
On CUDA, adapt only the request parameters in the constrained Python example to limit candidates from each parent while retaining width 128. This is also a fragment for an already configured engine with sufficient candidate capacity:

params = BeamSearchParams(
    beam_width=128,
    per_parent_beam_widths=[128, 8, 4],
    result_width=16,
    max_tokens=5,
    temperature=0.0,
    ignore_eos=True,
    begin_token="<|sid_begin|>",
    end_token="<|sid_end|>",
    include_stop_str_in_output=True,
)

The first candidate count equals the first retained width. Later retained widths cannot exceed the previous width times that stage's candidate count. Global selection still chooses the winners; no parent has a survival quota. HTTP carries the schedule in vllm_xargs.per_parent_beam_widths. There is no corresponding standalone-demo flag, and NPU rejects this schedule here.

For multiple CUDA catalogs, the Multi-Trie workflow uses tools/build_constraint_table.py --tries with a manifest of separately prepared triples documents. Use its emitted digests and constraint_table_v2 format, then pass one trie_ids value per prompt to the Python Beam call; completions HTTP uses vllm_xargs.trie_ids. Selectors are separate from BeamSearchParams.

All roots share one model vocabulary and tokenizer. Trie IDs start at zero and belong to the loaded artifact; choosing a root does not switch models. Omission selects root zero, while an out-of-range selector is rejected rather than becoming unconstrained. NPU currently accepts only one Trie and root zero. CPU compilation/reference support does not establish CPU Beam inference.

Measure each route with matching inputs and its own probability domain. See Validation and benchmarking and Troubleshooting for precision and graph diagnostics.

docs.title: Python API reference
docs.text: This page covers the public interfaces used by the first-release OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B guides. It is a curated reference for the pinned source snapshot, rather than an exhaustive mirror of every upstream vLLM class.

docs.title: GRLLM
docs.text:
from vllm_gr import GRLLM

GRLLM extends the installed vLLM LLM. Pass the local model and a canonical vllm_gr_config; supported native engine options pass through to vLLM. The complete Python example shows construction, request processing, and shutdown under a __main__ guard.

Interface Behavior get_tokenizer() Return the tokenizer used by this engine. beam_search_v1(prompts, params, ..., output_mode="compact") Return one final Beam result per input prompt. generate(...) Ordinary LLM generation, separate from GR SID Beam selection. shutdown() Release the engine; the context manager calls it on exit.

beam_search_v1() accepts token or text prompt structures. The tutorial uses vllm.inputs.tokens_input() after explicit tokenization. Optional call arguments include lora_request, use_tqdm, concurrency_limit, and trie_ids; availability remains subject to the chosen platform and engine contract. An argument in the signature does not establish every feature combination. In particular, lora_request is present in the signature, but current Beam V1 admission rejects LoRA requests.

The retired beam_search() frontend is not an alternative to V1. Do not pass removed catalog_path or constraint_backend constructor arguments alongside canonical configuration.

docs.title: BeamSearchParams
docs.text:
from vllm_gr.sampling_params import BeamSearchParams

params = BeamSearchParams(
    beam_width=128,
    max_tokens=5,
    temperature=0.0,
    ignore_eos=True,
    begin_token="<|sid_begin|>",
    end_token="<|sid_end|>",
    include_stop_str_in_output=True,
)

This is a request object, not a standalone inference program. Capacity 128 must already exist in the engine. Two boundary positions leave three effective generated components. See Beam parameters and modes for dynamic widths, result limits, candidate schedules, and platform restrictions.

docs.title: Output records
docs.text:
Mode Request result Candidate fields compact (default) sequences, shared prompt_token_ids token_ids, cumulative_logprob, finish_reason, stop_reason full Native-style lazy Beam output tokens, cum_logprob, and completion metadata

Compact token IDs contain the generated suffix without repeating the original prompt. Boundary/stop inclusion follows the request's output options; the tutorial explicitly includes its markers. Decode with the same tokenizer. Full tokens include the prompt and may materialize lazily. Select an output mode explicitly when measuring API time or consuming results.

The count is bounded by the requested return limit and legal candidates; capacity is not a promise of that many distinct returned items. An invalid request or a failed session is an error, not an empty successful accuracy test.

docs.text:
Function Result load_gr_config(path) Parse canonical YAML into GRConfig, resolving artifact paths against the file. gr_config_from_mapping(mapping) Validate a canonical mapping; artifact paths must be absolute without an explicit base directory. gr_config_to_mapping(config) Return canonical primitive values suitable for YAML/JSON. resolve_candidate_width(config) Resolve the configured candidate capacity.

docs.title: Async and HTTP boundaries
docs.text:
There is no exported GRAsyncLLM convenience class in this snapshot. Native AsyncLLM and the GR async adapters can be embedded without HTTP, but direct integration must own the request/session lifecycle. Do not write await GRLLM.beam_search_v1(...) around the synchronous API.

Use Python integration for the actual async entry points and Online serving for the supported HTTP walkthrough. HTTP Beam fields and response mapping are covered in Serving and batching.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: vLLM-GR adapts an installed vLLM runtime for generative recommendation. The first-release walkthrough uses OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B on CUDA or Ascend NPU. Pangu is documented separately as an NPU extension.

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
Python or HTTP frontend
        |
Input preparation + validation
        |
EngineCore admission
        |
Native scheduler + GR metadata
        |
Worker: Prefill / Decode
        |
Validated terminal result

The frontend submits a complete Beam batch and waits for its terminal result; it does not drive a Python token-by-token Beam loop. EngineCore admits the session, native scheduling owns prompt accounting and KV blocks, and Workers own device execution and generated Beam state.

docs.title: Ownership boundaries
docs.text:
Component Responsibility Frontend Tokenize/render inputs, validate public requests, submit and consume results. Canonical configuration Preserve engine-lifetime settings across processes. EngineCore Admit batches and own session progress. Scheduler Native request accounting and GR dispatch metadata. Worker and model runner Model forwards, candidate selection, parent state, KV inheritance, graphs. Constraint backend Artifact identity, legal token candidates, score-domain rules.

Prefill selects the first generated component. Later Decode forwards read the selected parents' KV histories before extending them. The parent mapping is a correctness contract, not only a memory-copy optimization. See Beam Search explained.

docs.title: Scheduling and lifecycle
docs.text:
The runtime distinguishes a business batch, each native request in that batch, and its physical Beam rows. One logical Decode token can execute many Beam rows. A dynamic retained width changes those row geometries without changing the engine's declared capacity.

Terminal results are delivered after the matching release confirmation. Completion, cancellation, and failure must drain owned work before reusing buffers. A frontend disconnect and complete device cleanup are different events; follow the actual lifecycle and transport contract.

All participating frontend, EngineCore, and Worker processes must use the same code/schema revision. The current Beam protocol does not support mixed-revision rolling upgrades; restart the deployment together.

docs.title: Platform and graph adapters
docs.text:
beam.execution_mode: v1 names the GR Beam protocol, independently of native ModelRunner V1/V2. The documented default is ModelRunner V1. CUDA's experimental V2 adaptation is not a general NPU support promise.

CUDA and NPU use different operator, storage, and graph adapters. A model forward graph does not imply that all candidate selection and KV operations are inside that same graph. Prefill capture and Beam Decode capture have separate controls. Verify replay and numerical behavior separately.

Top-level import vllm_gr is lightweight. Runtime initialization belongs to the GR plugin and explicit initialization path; successful frontend import alone does not prove that Worker patches or custom operators are active.

For implementation work, start with Developer guide, the source ownership map, and the batch lifecycle contract. The runtime patch inventory records patch ownership and activation.

docs.title: Beam Search explained
docs.text:
Beam Search keeps several possible continuations after each generated token. For recommendation, a continuation may contain semantic ID (SID) components such as A, B, and C. A catalog-constrained search accepts children that follow the supplied catalog; a full-vocabulary search has no item-membership guarantee.

This page explains the search and KV-cache relationship in the source snapshot used by these guides. Start with First offline inference, then use Beam parameters and modes for actual settings.

docs.title: Follow one generation stage
docs.text:
Each non-final stage connects five operations:

  1. Run the model for the current prefixes and produce logits.
  2. Select up to K valid candidate tokens for each parent.
  3. Add each parent's cumulative score and select the winning children globally.
  4. Carry each winner's parent index into sequence state and KV inheritance.
  5. Feed the selected child tokens to the next model forward.

The arrows carry token IDs, scores, and parent identity together. Keeping only the selected token IDs is insufficient: identical tokens can extend different prefixes and therefore require different attention histories.

docs.title: Separate capacity, candidate count, and returned results
docs.text:
Symbol Meaning Example C Engine storage capacity, configured by beam.max_width 128 w_in Number of parent prefixes entering this stage 64 K Maximum candidate tokens contributed by each parent 64 w_out Number of winning children retained after this stage 32 R Maximum final sequences returned to the caller 16 N Number of generated components in each fixed-budget sequence 3

Capacity 128 does not mean 128 generated tokens. It bounds the supported Beam geometry; the request's beam_width still matches the configured capacity. A dynamic schedule changes the active retained widths within that capacity. The candidate pool has up to w_in * K entries, including invalid slots that cannot win. There must be enough valid continuations to fill the intended result set; padding or invalid entries do not create valid recommendations.

R=16, N=3 means returning at most 16 sequences of three generated components. It does not mean 16 generation steps, nor does it narrow earlier search stages. Likewise, the demo's --print-beams changes only how many records are printed.

docs.title: Local TopK and global selection do different jobs
docs.text:
For parent p and candidate token x, the ordinary cumulative score is:

child_score(p, x) = parent_score(p) + log_probability(x | parent_prefix(p))

Local TopK limits each parent's candidate contribution. Global selection ranks the complete candidate pool for the request and retains w_out children. One parent may supply multiple winners; another may supply none. A per-parent candidate limit is not a quota that guarantees every parent a surviving child. Final length-penalty handling is separate from this cumulative-score example.

The following small examples use retained width W=3 and K=2 to make parent identity visible. They illustrate the algorithm, not a universal NPU configuration. In this source snapshot, independent per-parent candidate counts are exposed for CUDA V1; NPU has additional candidate-width restrictions.

docs.title: Two parents can produce three winning children
docs.text:
Suppose two prefixes remain, with cumulative scores P0=-1.00 and P1=-1.40:

Parent Candidate Conditional log probability Cumulative score Global rank P0 a -0.80 -1.80 1 P0 b -1.10 -2.10 2 P1 c -0.90 -2.30 3 P1 d -1.80 -3.20 4

Four candidates compete for three positions. The winning children are P0+a, P0+b, and P1+c, with parent indices [0, 0, 1]. This stage widens two parents into three children. It duplicates a parent's history where needed; it does not reconstruct a previously discarded prefix.

docs.title: Three parents still need a global competition
docs.text:
At a later stage, suppose the input scores are [-1.80, -2.10, -2.30]:

Parent Candidate Conditional log probability Cumulative score Global rank P0 e -0.70 -2.50 1 P0 f -0.90 -2.70 2 P1 g -2.00 -4.10 5 P1 h -2.20 -4.30 6 P2 i -0.80 -3.10 3 P2 j -1.50 -3.80 4

Six candidates compete for three positions. The winning parent map is [0, 0, 2]: P0 contributes twice, P1 is eliminated, and P2 contributes once. Some execution paths group survivors by parent for the next forward instead of storing them in score order. Tokens, scores, sequence state, and KV must all follow the same permutation; final output ranking is a separate boundary.

docs.title: Why selecting parents requires KV reordering
docs.text:
Attention reads K/V tensors representing the prefix already processed by the model. After selecting parent map [0, 0, 2], the next history must be:

new row 0 <- old parent 0 history
new row 1 <- old parent 0 history
new row 2 <- old parent 2 history
next input tokens = [e, f, i]

Rows 0 and 1 share the same past, but their next input tokens differ. On the next forward, those tokens create different new K/V entries. Reading the old row-1 history for child P0+f would combine the wrong prefix with the selected token and could change logits, scores, and later recommendations.

The prompt's paged KV can remain shared. The generated suffix's per-Beam KV must inherit the selected parent across every attention layer. A gather needs safe staging when source and destination overlap or a parent appears twice; an unsafe in-place overwrite can destroy history another child still needs.

KV reordering still happens where required. Its implementation depends on the execution path; do not identify the algorithm with one operator name:

Path in this source snapshot How parent KV inheritance is implemented NPU native fixed-width decision The eligible xllm path calls select_unshared_kv after non-final selection; a dispatcher provides the fallback. Dynamic stage-width state reorder_stage_kv gathers the selected parents into persistent pools for the target width, including repeated parents. CUDA persistent V1 runner Dedicated gather/scatter kernels apply the selected parent mapping.

The NPU native operator's grouped-parent, full-width assumptions must hold. Passing a new logical width to an old physical pool is not a substitute for correct pool strides. Dynamic execution maintains width-specific contiguous pools and their lifetimes. On the final selection, there is no next attention forward, so the NPU fixed/dynamic paths skip that next-step KV reorder.

docs.title: Narrowing and widening with capacity 128
docs.text:
Keep beam.max_width=128 and request beam_width=128. For a three-component SID, the retained-width schedules below express different searches:

Schedule After A After B After C Decode input widths Fixed 128 128 128 128, 128 Narrowing 128 64 32 128, 64 Widening 32 64 128 32, 64

Narrowing keeps fewer parents for later forwards. Widening branches from the parents that survived earlier selection; it cannot recover pruned prefixes. Both can change search results and recommendation quality relative to a fixed schedule. A larger final width does not make earlier pruning reversible.

These are examples within the three-step contract of this snapshot, not a claim that every device, width, candidate count, or longer schedule works. Use the parameter reference for platform restrictions and matching graph configuration, and check models and capabilities before changing modes.

docs.title: Prefill, Decode, and graphs
docs.text:
For three effective generated components, final prompt logits select A during Prefill. Decode 1 processes A to select B; Decode 2 processes B to select C. This V1 path requires Chunked Prefill to be disabled. The complete remaining prompt must fit the Prefill budget; the first generated component is selected from its final prompt logits.

Begin/end markers affect the public token budget. With both markers configured, max_tokens=5 reserves two positions and produces three searched components. See step counting.

Graph execution replays work against stable buffers and compatible shapes. It does not change the intended candidate scoring, global selection, parent identity, or KV inheritance rules. Capture coverage is path-specific: a Beam Forward graph does not imply that the LM head, TopK, and KV reorder are all inside that same graph. Prefill capture is configured separately from Decode.

For NPU, the graph key includes logical batch size and Decode input width. The widening example needs widths 32 and 64 for its two Decode forwards; the final retained width 128 has no following forward. Verify actual replay rather than inferring it from a graph flag. Different kernels can have floating-point differences, so intended mathematical equivalence still needs numerical checks. Use validation and benchmarking to compare tokens, scores, rankings, graph replay, and latency under matching inputs and settings.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: The vllm-gr command wraps the installed vLLM serving CLI and adds the GR configuration boundary. Run it in the same prepared CUDA or Ascend environment as the model. It does not provision accelerator drivers or vendor operators.

docs.text:

vllm-gr --version

The top-level subcommands in this snapshot are serve and check-env. Benchmarks and model/data preparation tools below are repository scripts, not invented vllm-gr bench or vllm-gr convert subcommands.

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
vllm-gr check-env

vllm-gr check-env --npu

The NPU option requires the active Ascend platform and checks the matching runtime pair and active Triton-Ascend backend. Success does not establish custom-operator execution, available device memory, or model accuracy.

docs.title: serve
docs.text:
Use Online serving for complete runnable CUDA/NPU commands. The form is vllm-gr serve MODEL --vllm-gr-config CONFIG [native options].

Option Owner and purpose Positional model Local model directory in the first-release walkthrough. --vllm-gr-config Canonical GR YAML; contains Beam/table configuration. --served-model-name Client-visible alias, onerec in the example. --host, --port HTTP bind address; examples bind to loopback. --async-scheduling Required scheduling policy for this V1 path. --no-enable-chunked-prefill Keep complete Prefill for Beam V1. --enforce-eager Native eager control; NPU first-run examples also disable Beam graphs in YAML. Native capacity/memory flags See Configuration reference.

Do not add legacy catalog, attention, or Beam overrides alongside canonical YAML. Restart the engine after changing engine-lifetime settings. More native arguments in --help do not imply GR support for every vLLM feature combination.

python tools/build_constraint_triples.py --help

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text: Use the canonical schema-v1 configuration for GR engine settings. Native vLLM options, Beam request parameters, and process environment variables have different owners. Start with Data and constraints to generate a configuration containing real artifact paths and digests.

docs.title: Configuration layers
docs.text:
Layer Python Serving GR engine lifetime vllm_gr_config mapping, YAML path, or GRConfig --vllm-gr-config YAML Native engine lifetime Supported GRLLM constructor options Native serve flags One Beam call BeamSearchParams and call arguments Completion fields and supported vllm_xargs Process/runtime Environment set before Python starts Environment inherited by server and Workers

Do not mix canonical configuration with legacy catalog, attention, or Beam overrides. Unknown canonical keys are errors. The parser does not expand shell variables in YAML strings: generate actual paths rather than writing $MODEL or $WORKDIR into a file and expecting shell interpolation later.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text:
Key Schema default or requirement Usage schema_version Required; 1 Select the canonical configuration schema. attention_backend Unset These Beam guides explicitly use CUSTOM. constrained_generation Unset Leave unset for the enabled catalog table; explicitly false selects the separate unconstrained path. beam Empty mapping Select the Beam interface and storage/graph policies below. constraint_table Mapping with required max_top_k An enabled table additionally needs its artifact identity.

Schema acceptance validates configuration structure; it does not prove device support, available memory, a readable artifact, matching weights, or inference.

docs.title: Beam engine keys
docs.text:
Key under beam Schema default Meaning execution_mode Unset Set v1 for beam_search_v1(). max_width Unset Persistent Beam capacity; match each request's width. Schema ceiling: 1024, with additional candidate/platform restrictions. max_decode_steps 3 Effective generation capacity, including the component selected by Prefill. This does not extend a three-level table. worker_decision Unset These V1 guides explicitly set true; platform admission still applies. graph_enabled true Enable the Beam Decode graph path when a Beam pool is configured. graph_batch_size 1 Exact NPU logical batch capture dimension, not scheduler capacity. graph_widths Unset Additional exact NPU Decode input widths; unique positive widths no greater than capacity. online_batch_sizes [1, 2, 4] Online batching policy; the first-run guides deliberately use [1]. Allowed logical sizes are 1 through 8. enable_short_suffix_attention true CUDA short-suffix attention optimization; not an NPU mode selector. prefill_flash_attn_version auto CUDA Prefill policy; accepted values are auto, null, 2, and 3. sid_stage_vocab false Opt into the NPU catalog-free A/B/C domain, with its separate requirements. engine_driven Retired Omit it. true is consumed with a warning; false is rejected.

The NPU graph policy allows at most eight captured widths including the implicit maximum-width bank when Beam graphs are active. Numeric schema ceilings are not a supported-shape matrix. Use Beam parameters and modes and Serving and batching before changing widths or batches.

docs.title: Constraint Table keys
docs.text:
Key under constraint_table Schema default or requirement Meaning max_top_k Required positive integer Candidate storage ceiling; execution and candidate limits still apply. enabled false Enable loading the canonical artifact. backend cuda Placement: cuda, npu, or cpu; CPU compilation/reference support is not production CPU Beam inference. path Unset Required for an enabled table; path to the saved .safetensors artifact. format constraint_table_v1 Three-level single-Trie format; constraint_table_v2 selects the separate multi-Trie format. artifact_digest Unset Required for an enabled table; use the builder's exact sha256: identity. tokenizer_digest Unset Required for an enabled table; use the builder's tokenizer identity. candidate_width Unset Independent scalar candidate count; platform and retained-width rules apply.

When candidate width is unset it follows the retained-width policy. Capacity above 256 requires an explicit candidate width within the candidate ceiling. The independent candidate count is capped at 256 even though the schema does not impose that same numeric ceiling on max_top_k. NPU has stricter width-equality requirements; do not copy a CUDA-only setting into an NPU configuration because its schema accepts the integer.

Paths in YAML resolve relative to that YAML file. A direct mapping requires an absolute artifact path unless the caller explicitly supplies a base directory to the parser. Digests validate compiled inputs; they are not model-weight checksums. Keep model, tokenizer, catalog, and mapping provenance separately.

docs.title: Inspect a prepared configuration
docs.text:
With GR_CONFIG exported by the data-preparation guide:

python - <<'PY'
import os
import yaml
from vllm_gr.config import gr_config_to_mapping, load_gr_config

config = load_gr_config(os.environ["GR_CONFIG"])
print(yaml.safe_dump(gr_config_to_mapping(config), sort_keys=False))
PY

This parses and normalizes configuration without loading model weights. It does not load the artifact or verify its contents against the model. Engine startup performs additional checks.

docs.title: Native engine and request options
docs.text:
These do not belong inside canonical beam or constraint_table:

Native option Purpose max_model_len Model context limit. max_num_batched_tokens Scheduling token budget, including complete remaining Prefill and physical NPU Decode row requirements. max_num_seqs Native logical-request capacity; separate from physical Decode token rows and the exact online batch policy. max_logprobs Budget that must cover the required candidate count. gpu_memory_utilization Device-memory allocation target, including on NPU. async_scheduling Keep enabled for this V1 path. enable_chunked_prefill Keep disabled for this V1 path. enforce_eager Native execution control; pair it with GR graph policy for the intended run.

Request width, generation budget, dynamic schedule, return limit, and boundary tokens are described in the Beam parameter reference. For additional_config platform extensions, use the installed vendor release's contract. The canonical GR schema does not accept arbitrary native or vendor keys, including enable_npugraph_ex.

Sources: canonical parser, configuration model, and validation rules, pinned to this site's source snapshot.

docs.title: Data and constraints
docs.text:
Model weights, tokenizers, catalogs, and business item mappings have different roles. This guide prepares one persistent Constraint Table and its canonical configuration for a local OneRec model on CUDA GPU or Ascend NPU.

Complete installation and model preparation first. Run commands in Bash from the vllm-gr source repository root, using the matching Python environment. On NPU, keep the CANN and custom operator environments loaded. Preparation compiles data; it does not run model inference.

docs.title: Keep the files distinct
docs.text:
Catalog JSON
    |
Triples + model config/tokenizer
    |
Constraint Table + digests
    |
YAML -> Python or HTTP

Generated SID
    |
Business mapping -> item(s)
Input or output Contents Used by Model directory Weights, model configuration, and tokenizer assets Model loading; compilation reads the config and tokenizer Raw catalog JSON A list of legal token-string sequences tools/build_constraint_triples.py Triples JSON A/B/C token strings, sentinel metadata, and relations tools/build_constraint_table.py; the offline Beam demo .safetensors artifact Compiled token-ID relations and metadata The configured Constraint Table loader Canonical YAML Artifact identity and GR execution settings Python vllm_gr_config or --vllm-gr-config SID-to-item mapping Business identifiers and any mapping-selection metadata Your application or task evaluator

The repository does not include model weights. Download them separately and keep the weights, configuration, and tokenizer from the same snapshot. Compiling a catalog does not train embeddings, update model weights, or teach the model which items a user prefers.

docs.title: 1. Set the model, output directory, and backend
docs.text:
Use the existing local OneRec snapshot from the first-inference guide. Adjust MODEL if it is stored elsewhere:

export MODEL="$PWD/models/OneRec-1.7B"
export WORKDIR="$PWD/results/data-preparation"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"
test -d "$MODEL"
test -f "$MODEL/config.json"

Choose the backend that will run inference:

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
export BACKEND=cuda

export BACKEND=npu

The backend selects the runtime loader in the generated configuration. It does not turn the table into model weights or establish device execution coverage.

docs.title: 2. Choose one triples input route
docs.text: Run either route A or route B, then continue with the common compilation step. Do not pass an arbitrary raw catalog to the artifact builder.

docs.title: Route A: reuse the repository's example triples
docs.text:
For the shortest preparation path:

export CATALOG="$PWD/tools/AB_Tests/constraints/video_constraint_triples.json"
test -f "$CATALOG"

This file is already a triples document. Do not run the raw-catalog converter on it. Its name and the offline demo's --catalog argument do not mean every JSON file is accepted. The fixture is useful for execution checks; it is not a substitute for your business catalog, item mapping, or evaluation dataset.

docs.title: Route B: convert a raw catalog
docs.text:
A raw catalog is a JSON list of sequences, not a mapping of token IDs to item IDs. This small format example contains two distinct legal triples:

cat > "$WORKDIR/catalog.json" <<'JSON'
[
  ["<|sid_begin|>", "<s_a_1>", "<s_b_2>", "<s_c_3>", "<|sid_end|>"],
  ["<|sid_begin|>", "<s_a_1>", "<s_b_2>", "<s_c_4>", "<|sid_end|>"]
]
JSON

export CATALOG="$WORKDIR/constraint_triples.json"
python tools/build_constraint_triples.py \
  --catalog "$WORKDIR/catalog.json" \
  --output "$CATALOG" \
  --begin '<|sid_begin|>' \
  --end '<|sid_end|>'

For real use, replace the input file with your model-aligned catalog before conversion. The two-row example can return at most two distinct complete SID paths; Beam width 128 does not create more legal items.

The converter validates sequence shape, sentinel consistency, and exactly three semantic components, and rejects duplicate A/B/C triples. If every input sequence contains only the three components, omit --begin and --end. Use consistent wrapping within a catalog. Let the tool generate the document's format_version, triples, sentinels, and relations fields.

Triples store token strings, not tokenizer IDs. The artifact compiler maps them using the selected tokenizer and model vocabulary size. Each catalog symbol must be a registered vocabulary entry with a valid, unambiguous token ID; an unknown token silently mapped to UNK is not a valid SID registration. Adding strings to the catalog does not add tokenizer entries or weight rows.

docs.title: 3. Compile once and write the canonical configuration
docs.text:
Both routes now provide CATALOG, a triples document. Run this common step once. It calls the real artifact builder used by the CLI and writes the resulting path and digests into YAML, avoiding manual copying:

python - <<'PY'
import os
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
from tools.build_constraint_table import build_constraint_table
from vllm_gr.config import gr_config_from_mapping

backend = os.environ["BACKEND"]
if backend not in {"cuda", "npu"}:
    raise ValueError("BACKEND must be cuda or npu")
model = Path(os.environ["MODEL"]).resolve(strict=True)
if not model.is_dir():
    raise ValueError("MODEL must be a local model directory")
work = Path(os.environ["WORKDIR"]).resolve()
work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
artifact = work / "video_constraint_table.safetensors"
artifact_digest, tokenizer_digest, vocab_size = build_constraint_table(
    triples_path=os.environ["CATALOG"],
    model=str(model),
    revision=None,
    output_path=artifact,
    trust_remote_code=True,
)
config = {
    "schema_version": 1,
    "attention_backend": "CUSTOM",
    "beam": {
        "execution_mode": "v1",
        "graph_enabled": backend == "cuda",
        "graph_batch_size": 1,
        "online_batch_sizes": [1],
        "worker_decision": True,
        "max_width": 128,
        "max_decode_steps": 3,
    },
    "constraint_table": {
        "enabled": True,
        "backend": backend,
        "max_top_k": 128,
        "path": str(artifact),
        "format": "constraint_table_v1",
        "artifact_digest": artifact_digest,
        "tokenizer_digest": tokenizer_digest,
    },
}
gr_config_from_mapping(config)
config_path = work / "vllm_gr_config.yaml"
config_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(config, sort_keys=False), encoding="utf-8")
print(f"config={config_path}")
print(f"artifact_digest={artifact_digest}")
print(f"tokenizer_digest={tokenizer_digest}")
print(f"vocab_size={vocab_size}")
PY

export GR_CONFIG="$WORKDIR/vllm_gr_config.yaml"
test -f "$GR_CONFIG"

This is the Python entry point of tools/build_constraint_table.py, not a second builder you must run afterward. Keep the artifact and YAML together. The YAML sets capacity 128, three effective generated components, a single HTTP batch size, and no independent candidate-width override. CUDA retains its graph path; NPU Beam graphs are disabled for the initial configuration. For a fully eager NPU run, also use the engine's enforce_eager=True or serving --enforce-eager, as shown in Online serving.

The example uses a local model directory, so revision=None is intentional. The builder requires a revision for a remote model ID and resolves a symbolic revision before loading the tokenizer and configuration. For reproducible builds, preserve the local snapshot and record its immutable model revision.

docs.title: Understand the two digests
docs.text:
Value Identifies Does not establish artifact_digest SHA-256 of the complete saved artifact bytes Recommendation quality or model-weight identity tokenizer_digest The canonical vocabulary, added vocabulary, and special-token role/ID state used by the compiler A checksum of the model's learned weights vocab_size Model-config vocabulary dimension used to validate IDs and load the table That arbitrary replacement weights are equivalent

Use the returned digests exactly, including their sha256: prefix. The loader checks the artifact format, expected digest, tokenizer digest, and vocabulary size. Do not edit a digest to silence a mismatch. Rebuild the artifact and YAML when the catalog or tokenizer changes, and keep a separate record of the model weights and source revision. A moved file with unchanged bytes is different from a changed tokenizer or catalog behind the same path.

The offline demo still compiles its own temporary table from --catalog; it does not automatically consume GR_CONFIG. Use the persistent table with the Python integration or the service's --vllm-gr-config. The latter still needs native engine settings such as asynchronous scheduling and disabled Chunked Prefill; this YAML alone is not a complete launch command.

docs.title: Map a complete SID back to business items
docs.text:
The generated <s_a_1><s_b_2><s_c_3> symbols describe a complete SID. The numbers 1, 2, and 3 are SID components, not their tokenizer vocabulary IDs. The Constraint Table checks allowed combinations; it does not return business item details or contain the SID-to-item mapping's values.

The OpenOneRec conversion convention encodes component values as:

encoded_sid = A * 8192 * 8192 + B * 8192 + C

The dataset's sid2pid.json maps these encoded SID keys to item records; the product task uses sid2iid.json. One SID may map to several items, so the task's selection strategy and mapping metadata matter. This base-8192 convention belongs to that dataset, not to every model or catalog.

The repository's dataset catalog converter reads the mapping's keys to produce token sequences. Keep the original mapping: the resulting catalog/triples do not retain its item records. Use the matching dataset release, task, item-selection policy, and ground truth when evaluating recommendations. A legal SID, or a randomly initialized SID checkpoint that executes successfully, does not establish useful recommendations or Recall.

Continue with Python integration to load this exact configuration from an application, or use Online serving, Beam parameters and modes, or Validation and benchmarking. For input, digest, and tokenizer failures, see Troubleshooting.

The pinned sources are the triples converter, artifact builder, artifact loader, and tokenizer digest contract.

docs.title: Developer guide
docs.text: vLLM-GR extends an installed vLLM runtime. Begin with the selected platform's CUDA installation or Ascend installation, then use this guide to find the owning code before changing behavior. The main model walkthrough uses OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B; model weights are separate inputs.

docs.title: Prepare the actual development runtime
docs.text:
Run commands from the inference repository root, in an environment prepared for the device. On Ascend, retain the vendor runtime and loaded CANN/xllm-ops environment; installing the GR package does not provision those dependencies.

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
VLLM_GR_TARGET_DEVICE=cuda pip install -e ".[dev]"
vllm-gr check-env

VLLM_GR_TARGET_DEVICE=npu pip install -e ".[dev]" --no-build-isolation
vllm-gr check-env --npu

Confirm which checkout the interpreter imports before runtime validation:

python --version
python -c 'import vllm_gr; print(vllm_gr.__file__)'
git rev-parse HEAD

A sibling source directory is a reference, not proof of the imported package. Keep version constraints in pyproject.toml, setup.py, requirements/, and vllm_gr/_env_check.py aligned. check-env does not run a model or establish that an accelerator has enough free memory. Follow testing and CI for the checks appropriate to the change.

docs.title: Find the owner and contract
docs.text:
Change Code owner Read first Package initialization and runtime patches vllm_gr/plugin.py, patch.py, _env_check.py Patch inventory Configuration and offline Python API vllm_gr/config/, entrypoints/gr.py Python integration, parameters HTTP/gRPC, admission, scheduling, cleanup vllm_gr/entrypoints/, v1/engine/ Batch lifecycle contract Beam state, selection, parent lineage vllm_gr/v1/beam/ Decision contract, Beam explanation Worker, Attention, and graphs vllm_gr/v1/worker/, v1/attention/backends/, ops/ Development map, Prefill graph contract Catalog artifacts and candidate scoring vllm_gr/constraints/, tools/build_constraint_table.py Data and constraints, scoring implementation Platform registration and activation vllm_gr/platforms/ Platform backend contract

The frontend submits a logical batch and waits for the terminal result. EngineCore owns session progress, native scheduling owns prompt accounting and paged KV blocks, and Workers own device state. Preserve those ownership boundaries, including failure, cancellation, retirement, and resource release. Increasing storage capacity does not grant additional concurrent owners.

docs.title: Preserve platform and patch boundaries
docs.text:
Top-level import vllm_gr stays lightweight. Runtime initialization belongs to plugin.initialize_runtime() and the general-plugin entry point. Main, EngineCore, and Worker processes initialize independently; a frontend-only check does not prove that a spawned Worker installed its hooks.

Provider registration must avoid hardware imports. Activation, environment checking, runtime compatibility patches, Worker hooks, and Attention dispatch are distinct boundaries. Use the canonical device names cuda and npu. Read the platform contract before changing fallback or import behavior.

When changing patch targets, ownership, activation, or removal, update both docs/runtime_patch_inventory.md and docs/patch_inventory.yaml, together with the relevant contract coverage. Do not hand-edit generated gRPC bindings or vllm_gr/_version.py; use the owning generation/build procedure. Beam protocol V1 and ModelRunner V1/V2 are separate selections. Preserve ordinary non-GR inference when modifying a shared patch or transport.

docs.title: Prepare a reviewable contribution
docs.text:
1. Read the checkout's AGENTS.md, Contributing, and owning contract.
  2. Make a focused branch and keep unrelated edits out of the change.
  3. Reproduce a bug before its fix when practical, then verify the same case.
  4. Update affected public examples and contracts, and select meaningful checks.
  5. Describe the problem, resulting behavior, exact validation, and remaining gaps.

Use the inference repository's PR template. Keep passed, failed, skipped, and unrun coverage separate. Functional output, graph replay, recommendation accuracy, and latency are different forms of evidence. For device results, retain the imported revision, runtime/device/model identity, configuration, command, and artifact paths.

Commit with your correct Git identity and a DCO sign-off, for example git commit -s. The configured commit-message hook also adds a Signed-off-by line when needed; inspect the final commit rather than assuming the hook ran. Do not claim authorship or validation performed by someone else.

docs.title: Keep inference development separate from website publication
docs.text: The rules above describe contributions to the inference repository. A separate documentation publication repository may hold generated website output and use different build/deployment checks. Publishing a site does not grant runtime repository write access or make the documentation source publicly editable. Use the actual source repository and its permissions when proposing edits; do not edit generated HTML as a substitute for changing the maintained source.

docs.title: Content ownership
docs.text:
This website presents an independent documentation edition for the source snapshot listed on the homepage. The publication repository currently contains generated HTML and static assets. It is separate from the inference source repository.

The information architecture follows the main categories of the vLLM-Omni documentation: user and developer guides, API/CLI references, and community information. The content and support scope here belong to vLLM-GR.

Shared documentation-source publication and its contributor build workflow: to be defined. Do not assume the publication repository already contains the Markdown sources or an automatic Markdown build pipeline.

docs.title: Report a documentation problem
docs.text:
Use a documentation issue with the page URL, incorrect sentence or command, installed source/runtime revision, and the expected behavior. Include the smallest relevant error when a command fails, with private paths and credentials removed.

For an inference bug, use the project links in Community. Changing a generated page does not change the framework runtime.

docs.title: Content review standard
docs.text:
• Use actual model names, canonical parameters, and the owning source contract.
  • Keep runnable examples distinct from fragments and future placeholders.
  • Distinguish import, schema, functional, graph, numerical, Recall, and timing evidence.
  • Check commands, links, code copying, search, themes, and mobile layout.
  • Preserve platform limits and version scope when adapting an upstream guide.
  • Leave unconfirmed project roles and plans clearly marked as pending.

Inference-repository Markdown follows its own documentation checks. Those checks do not by themselves establish that a rendered website or an accelerator example works.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: This is a focused reference for the variables used by these guides at source snapshot c4966f18, not an inventory of every upstream vLLM or vendor setting. Set runtime variables in the launching shell before Python starts, so EngineCore and Worker processes inherit them. Restart the engine after changing startup policy; changing a shell variable does not reconfigure a running process.

docs.title: Installation target is separate from runtime selection
docs.text:
VLLM_GR_TARGET_DEVICE controls the source package's installation/build target. The tutorials use cuda or npu; when unset, the build performs its documented device detection. Set the target explicitly when installing for a platform, as shown in the installation guides.

This variable does not install an accelerator driver, create the Ascend vendor stack, select a physical device, or force a different runtime platform. Runtime backend activation follows vLLM's selected current_platform.device_type. For example, setting VLLM_GR_TARGET_DEVICE=npu cannot make a CUDA-only Python environment serve NPU requests. See the build selection and runtime activation separately.

docs.title: Model runner and worker processes
docs.text:
Variable Behavior in this source Tutorial use VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER GR defaults an unset value to 0. Explicit truthy values are normalized to 1 and preserved as experimental opt-in. Use 0 for the default ModelRunner V1 guides. NPU unconstrained Beam rejects V2. VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD Controls the upstream worker start method. The GR NPU patch forces spawn when the parent has already initialized NPU. Explicitly use spawn in the Python integration examples.

The Beam protocol name beam_search_v1() is separate from the native model runner version. Opting into V2 does not establish support for every Beam mode. See Models and capabilities.

After saving the complete example from Python integration, launch it as a file rather than from Python standard input:

export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
python -u "$WORKDIR/python_beam.py"

Keep its if __name__ == "__main__" guard. Selecting spawn does not make an unguarded engine construction safe to execute repeatedly in child processes.

docs.title: Prefill graphs and NPU SID projection
docs.text:
Variable Behavior Boundary VLLM_ENABLE_PREFILL_CUDAGRAPH Gates the GR Prefill graph path. The GR flag defaults to enabled; use 0 to disable or 1 to allow it. Its value is cached at module import. Separate from beam.graph_enabled, which controls Beam Decode graphs. Native eager settings, supported shapes, and other execution checks still apply. VLLM_GR_NPU_STAGE_LM_HEAD Unset or exactly 1 allows the stage-projection optimization when its eligibility checks pass. 0 disables that optimization. Only relevant to the NPU catalog-free SID stage path; it does not enable that domain by itself.

Enabling a Prefill flag does not prove any particular shape captured or replayed. Turning it off is useful when isolating Decode behavior under the documented NPU padded-Prefill precision limitation. Read Validation and benchmarking before interpreting replay counters or numerical comparisons.

The NPU stage domain is selected through canonical constrained_generation: false and beam.sid_stage_vocab: true, with its other requirements. Disabling only the projection retains the same A/B/C families and score domain; it does not restore full-vocabulary probabilities. Use a fresh process for a reference/optimized comparison. See Advanced Beam workflows.

enable_npugraph_ex is not a GR environment variable documented by this page, nor an arbitrary top-level GRLLM argument. Platform configuration must follow the installed vLLM-Ascend release's actual configuration contract. Do not invent an environment spelling or copy it into canonical GR YAML. See Configuration reference.

docs.title: Accelerator visibility
docs.text:
The repository's CUDA examples and runners use CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; Ascend examples and runners use ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Set the appropriate variable according to your host/container allocation process before launching Python. These variables are interpreted by the corresponding runtime, not as GR catalog or Beam settings.

Do not assume that an example index names the same physical device across hosts, containers, visibility lists, or management tools. Check the allocation with your environment's documented procedure. A visible device may still lack enough free memory for the workload. The troubleshooting guide explains startup memory errors without terminating other users' processes.

docs.title: Example path variables are not engine options
docs.text:
Tutorial variable Meaning MODEL Local model snapshot, including weights and tokenizer assets. CATALOG Triples JSON consumed by the example or artifact builder. WORKDIR Directory for generated inputs, configuration, and results. GR_CONFIG Path to the canonical YAML generated by the data guide. BACKEND The example's cuda/npu choice, checked against its configuration and runtime.

These are shell/Python example conventions. The examples read them explicitly; they are not automatic runtime overrides. BACKEND=npu cannot change an engine already configured for CUDA. YAML strings containing $WORKDIR are not expanded by the GR parser; generate actual paths as in Data and constraints. Set variables again in a new terminal instead of assuming another shell's values were inherited.

When reporting an issue, share only the relevant variable names and sanitized values. Do not dump the entire environment, credential files, or authorization headers. For a small diagnostic record, use Troubleshooting.

Sources: runner policy, NPU spawn handling, Prefill graph flag, stage-projection gate, and device selection in the repository runner.

docs.title: Which model should I use first?
docs.text: Use OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B and its tokenizer, as in Quickstart. This first documentation edition presents it as the main CUDA/NPU recommendation model. Pangu is an additional NPU-only guide; it is not part of the GPU model walkthrough.

docs.title: Are model weights included in the repository?
docs.text: No. Download them separately. Keep configuration, weights, and tokenizer from the same snapshot. The bundled triples fixture is catalog data, not a model. See Data and constraints.

docs.title: Are catalog JSON, triples JSON, and the artifact interchangeable?
docs.text: No. Raw catalogs contain token-string sequences; the converter writes triples and relations. The artifact builder combines triples with a tokenizer and model vocabulary dimension. The online service loads the resulting .safetensors artifact, while the standalone offline demo compiles a temporary table itself.

docs.title: Does Beam width 128 mean generating 128 tokens?
docs.text: No. It is search/storage capacity. With the OneRec begin and end positions, max_tokens=5 searches three SID components. A return limit changes the final sequence count; --print-beams only changes display. See the parameter reference.

docs.title: Does a candidate limit preserve every parent?
docs.text: No. Parents contribute candidates that still compete globally. A parent may produce several winners or none. The selected parent indices must also govern KV inheritance. See Beam Search explained.

docs.title: Can dynamic Beam both narrow and widen?
docs.text: Yes, within the current capacity and platform rules. Widening branches from surviving prefixes; it cannot recover previously pruned prefixes. Changing the schedule changes the search and can change recommendation quality.

docs.title: Does a graph-enabled flag prove graph execution or equal scores?
docs.text: No. Check actual captures, dispatches, and fallback reasons. Numerical parity needs a separate comparison. In particular, the recorded NPU padded-Prefill limitation is not resolved by passing an exact-bucket test. See Validation and benchmarking.

docs.title: Is offline inference always synchronous?
docs.text: The public GRLLM.beam_search_v1() call is synchronous, while its engine uses asynchronous scheduling internally. Async engine integration can also run without HTTP, but this snapshot has no exported GRAsyncLLM convenience class. See Python integration.

docs.title: Does a valid SID prove recommendation accuracy?
docs.text: No. A catalog constrains legality. Recall needs the correct dataset, business mapping, and acceptance policy. Pangu's random SID conversion can exercise the execution path without supplying trained recommendation knowledge.

docs.title: Why can fewer than 128 candidates be returned?
docs.text: The valid catalog or configured result limit may be smaller than capacity. Invalid slots do not create recommendations. A failed request or a session with no valid final beams must be investigated as an error.

docs.title: Does CI mean hardware accuracy and performance passed?
docs.text: CI means continuous integration. A particular job may only check formatting, schema, packaging, or collection. Read the actual jobs, skips, hardware inputs, and evidence. See Testing and CI.

docs.title: Where are Maintainers and Committers listed?
docs.text: Those roles have not been finalized for this documentation edition. The governance page reserves their sections without assigning names or inferring roles from PR counts, repository access, or documentation ownership.

docs.title: First offline inference
docs.text:
New to the project? Follow Quickstart for the installation and first-run sequence. This page contains the detailed commands and output guide.

Run a single constrained OneRec Beam Search request on CUDA or Ascend NPU. This guide uses the repository's example constraint data, a short prompt, batch size 1, Beam width 128, and three generated SID components.

Complete the CUDA installation or Ascend NPU installation first. Run every command below in a Bash shell from the vllm-gr repository root, using that installation's Python environment. For Ascend, stay inside the prepared vendor container and load the CANN and custom xllm-ops environments described in the installation guide.

docs.title: 1. Check the runtime
docs.text:
Select an available accelerator using your environment's device allocation rules, then check the installed packages:

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
nvidia-smi
vllm-gr check-env

npu-smi info
vllm-gr check-env --npu

check-env checks runtime compatibility; it does not run a model or prove that enough device memory is available. Avoid devices occupied by other inference jobs.

docs.title: 2. Prepare the model and prompt
docs.text:
The framework repository does not include model weights. Download OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B, or point MODEL at an existing local copy of that model. Keep the weights, configuration, and tokenizer from the same snapshot.

export MODEL="$PWD/models/OneRec-1.7B"
export WORKDIR="$PWD/results/first-inference"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"

If the model is not already available, download it with the installed huggingface_hub library. This resolves one immutable model revision and uses it for the entire download. Keep the printed revision with your run records.

python - <<'PY'
import os
from huggingface_hub import HfApi, snapshot_download

repo = "OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B"
revision = HfApi().model_info(repo).sha
snapshot_download(repo_id=repo, revision=revision, local_dir=os.environ["MODEL"])
print(f"model_revision={revision}")
PY

See the Hugging Face download guide for authentication and download options.

Use the example triples document already tracked in the source repository:

export CATALOG="$PWD/tools/AB_Tests/constraints/video_constraint_triples.json"
export PROMPT="$WORKDIR/prompt.txt"

cat > "$PROMPT" <<'EOF'
Video history: <|sid_begin|><s_a_346><s_b_6566><s_c_5603><|sid_end|>.
Recommend the next video.
EOF

test -f "$MODEL/config.json"
test -f "$CATALOG"
test -f "$PROMPT"

This prompt and example catalog check that the inference path works. Use your own model-aligned catalog, representative prompts, and an evaluation dataset to measure recommendation quality or Recall.

docs.title: 3. Run Beam Search
docs.text:
Choose the tab matching your installed runtime:

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --catalog "$CATALOG" \
  --prompt "$PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend cuda \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 \
  --input-len 128 --generated-steps 3 \
  --print-beams 5

python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --catalog "$CATALOG" \
  --prompt "$PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend npu --execution eager \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 \
  --input-len 128 --generated-steps 3 \
  --print-beams 5

The script compiles a temporary Constraint Table from the triples document and the model tokenizer, loads the model, and calls GRLLM.beam_search_v1(). The temporary artifact is removed when the script exits. Startup, compilation, and graph capture can make the first run slower than later requests.

Setting Meaning in this example --model A local model directory, including its tokenizer and weights. --catalog A triples JSON document, not an arbitrary catalog JSON or a .safetensors artifact. --batch-size 1 Submit one prompt. Larger batches repeat the same prepared prompt in this script. --beam-width 128 Set both engine Beam capacity and request width to 128. --generated-steps 3 Generate the A, B, and C SID components; the first component comes from Prefill. --input-len 128 Prepare 127 prompt tokens, then let V1 append the begin token. Long inputs are truncated from the left; short inputs are left-padded with newline tokens. --print-beams 5 Print at most five returned candidates without reducing the search width.

The example sets asynchronous scheduling, disables Chunked Prefill, and keeps request width and engine capacity consistent. Keep the first run unchanged before adjusting advanced options.

Execution modes

--execution only controls the NPU path. The NPU command above starts in eager mode. After it works, change --execution eager to --execution graph to check NPU Decode graph capture and replay; this three-step run prints npu_beam_graph counters and fails if the expected replay is not observed. This option does not disable CUDA's existing graph behavior. A successful graph run establishes execution, not identical scores for every input shape.

docs.title: 4. Read the output
docs.text:
For each request, the script prints request=0 returned_beams=..., followed by JSON records for the first few candidates:

Field Meaning request, rank Request index and candidate rank, starting at zero. cumulative_logprob The candidate's cumulative log probability. sid_token_ids The trailing generated SID slice as token IDs. sid_tokens The same slice as token strings. For this three-step example, expect begin, A, B, C, and end positions. finish_reason, stop_reason Completion metadata from the Beam output.

The returned count depends on valid candidates and can be smaller than the requested width. SID components identify a catalog item through the matching SID-to-item mapping; they are not natural-language recommendation explanations. Scores and rankings are not fixed reference values across devices or batch shapes.

docs.title: 5. Prepare a reusable Constraint Table (optional)
docs.text:
For the complete catalog-to-artifact workflow, follow Data and constraints. To use the artifact in your own program, continue with Python integration.

For an application that loads a persistent artifact, compile it separately:

python tools/build_constraint_table.py \
  --triples "$CATALOG" \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --output "$WORKDIR/video_constraint_table.safetensors" \
  --trust-remote-code

The command prints artifact_digest, tokenizer_digest, and vocab_size. Use the artifact's absolute path and both digests in your application's constraint_table configuration. Rebuild it when the tokenizer or constraint data changes. The standalone script above always compiles its own temporary artifact; it does not read this saved file.

For the full dataset-to-catalog conversion, follow the OneRec data preparation guide. See the configuration reference for artifact fields and platform settings.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom What to check FileNotFoundError for the model, catalog, or prompt Run from the repository root and check the absolute paths exported above. Weights must be downloaded separately. tee: ... No such file or directory Create the log's parent directory before piping output to tee. Tokenizer or Constraint Table validation error Use a model with the matching SID tokens and compile with that exact tokenizer snapshot. Free device memory is below the requested utilization Select a free device or reduce --gpu-memory-utilization if enough memory remains for the workload. The default is 0.5, including on NPU. NPU custom operators cannot load Reload the CANN and xllm-ops environments from the Ascend installation guide in the active shell. NPU graph capture or replay is not observed Confirm the eager command works first, then keep the same inputs and select --execution graph.

This guide covers three-component constrained Beam Search. Unconstrained generation, thinking, dynamic Beam schedules, and multi-Trie inputs have separate configuration contracts; do not combine their options with the first-run command. Use the troubleshooting guide for diagnosis and Models and capabilities before switching modes.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Start here to run your first OneRec Beam Search request on CUDA GPU or Ascend NPU. Follow the steps in order: install your platform runtime, prepare the model and inputs, run one offline request, then inspect the returned SID candidates.

Already installed? Go straight to model and input preparation. If you have also prepared those inputs, jump to the offline run command.

docs.title: What you will run
docs.text:
Use a local OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B snapshot and its tokenizer with the repository's example video constraint data. Submit one prompt, keep Beam width 128, and generate three SID components: A, B, and C. The output is a ranked set of SID candidates.

This is a functional first run. Recommendation quality and performance need representative data and separate validation.

docs.title: 1. Install for your platform
docs.text:
Choose the platform on which the model will actually run:

  • CUDA GPU

    Prepare the CUDA runtime and install vLLM-GR with the supported vLLM 0.30 dependencies.

    Install on CUDA GPU

  • Ascend NPU

    Start inside the supported vLLM-Ascend vendor container, build and load xllm-ops, then install vLLM-GR.

    Install on Ascend NPU

Use the matching Python environment for every remaining step. On NPU, keep the CANN and custom operator environments loaded in the active shell. Run the inference commands from the vllm-gr source repository root on your accelerator host.

docs.title: 2. Prepare the model and inputs
docs.text:
Follow Prepare the model and prompt to download the weights, select the bundled triples document, and create the short example prompt. This step sets the MODEL, CATALOG, and PROMPT variables used by the run commands.

The model weights are downloaded separately. Keep the weights, configuration, and tokenizer from the same snapshot. The triples document is input to the example's Constraint Table compiler, rather than a model checkpoint.

docs.title: 3. Run one offline request
docs.text:
Open Run Beam Search, select the tab for your installed platform, and run its command in the same shell as step 2. Keep batch size 1, width 128, and three SID components for this first request.

The example compiles a temporary table automatically. You do not need to build or configure a persistent artifact for this offline run. The NPU command starts in eager mode; try graph execution after the basic request works.

Run the offline example

docs.title: 4. Check the result
docs.text:
The script prints a request summary in this form:

request=0 returned_beams=...

It then prints the leading candidate records, including sid_tokens and cumulative_logprob. For the three-component example, the SID slice has begin, A, B, C, and end positions. The actual count, token IDs, scores, and ranking depend on the inputs and runtime; a smaller valid candidate set can return fewer than 128 sequences.

Use Read the output to interpret these fields, or Troubleshooting if startup or inference fails.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Term Meaning in these guides SID Semantic identifier represented by token components such as A/B/C. Catalog The legal recommendation token sequences for a task. Constraint Table A compiled representation of legal token relations, tied to tokenizer identity. Trie A prefix structure; independent catalog roots share a tokenizer in a multi-Trie artifact. Beam capacity Engine storage limit, configured by beam.max_width. Retained width Number of winning prefixes kept after one generation stage. Candidate width / K Number of candidate tokens contributed per parent before global selection. TopK Selection of high-scoring candidates; per-parent and global selections have different roles. Parent index Identifies the prefix whose sequence and KV history a child inherits. KV cache Previously computed attention key/value state. Shared prefix Prompt/history KV that multiple Beams can read. Unshared suffix Per-Beam generated KV that follows selected parent ownership. Prefill Model work over the remaining input prompt; its final logits select the first generated component. Decode A later model forward extending generated prefixes. Eager Execution without replaying the selected graph path. Graph capture / replay Record work for compatible stable buffers/shapes, then replay it. FULL / fallback Dispatch-path evidence; a Beam FULL fallback need not be pure eager execution. Compact output Generated-tail CPU IDs and scores, with the original prompt stored once per request. Full output Native-style lazy Beam sequences that include the original prompt. P50 / P95 Median and 95th-percentile latency under a stated measurement boundary. E2E End-to-end within an explicitly defined API/client scope; not automatically kernel-only time. Recall Dataset-based recommendation quality requiring matching ground truth and item mappings. CoT / thinking A model's reasoning continuation, separate from constrained SID Beam selection. CI Continuous integration: automated checks whose coverage depends on the selected jobs. RFC Request for comments: a proposal for design discussion, separate from the implementing PR. PR Pull request: a reviewable repository change. Maintainer / Committer Project roles; names and governance are reserved in the governance page.

For the complete selection/KV flow, read Beam Search explained. For operational distinctions, use Metrics and logging.
