docs.title: Metrics and logging
docs.text: Use logs to establish what executed, metrics to observe the running service, and controlled benchmarks to measure a change. These are complementary inputs. Start with the one-request Online serving example before collecting a busy server's statistics.

docs.title: Health, model identity, and native metrics
docs.text:
In the client shell, with API and WORKDIR set as in the serving guide:

mkdir -p "$WORKDIR/diagnostics"
curl --fail --silent --show-error "$API/health"
curl --fail --silent --show-error "$API/v1/models" \
  --output "$WORKDIR/diagnostics/models.json"
curl --fail --silent --show-error "$API/metrics" \
  --output "$WORKDIR/diagnostics/metrics.txt"

The native vLLM metrics endpoint remains available in the documented server path. Its request metrics do not provide measured GR Beam stage durations. Keep the metric names, labels, server revision, and time window with any export. Server-wide activity is not automatically attributable to one client run.

docs.title: Beam phase metrics are not currently exported
docs.text:
This V1 source does not automatically export the historical vllm_gr_beam_search_* Prefill/Decode/sort collectors. Missing stage counters mean the phase measurement is unavailable, not that the phase took zero time. Do not reconstruct device stage latency from unrelated native request totals.

Older benchmark tools may accept historical counters when a server provides the complete required series. Counter resets, incomplete labels, or changed series invalidate a delta window. Do not silently turn missing data into a successful comparison. See the metrics contract.

docs.title: Useful log evidence
docs.text:
Question Evidence Which runtime loaded? Versions, model and tokenizer snapshot, imported checkout, selected platform. Why did startup fail? The first specific EngineCore/Worker error before the final initialization summary. Did a prompt list run as one batch? GR batch/session acceptance or decline logs; HTTP success alone does not prove fused batch execution. Did NPU Beam graphs replay? captured_shapes, full_dispatches, fallbacks, and fallback_reasons. How long did the request take? A defined API/client timing boundary and repeated measurements.

Graph counters include warmup when the engine uses it. A Beam FULL fallback does not necessarily mean a purely eager forward. Do not subtract counts from unrelated processes or infer a Decode replay for a one-component request.

docs.title: Latency and profiling
docs.text:
The offline benchmark reports batch API latency through returned output objects, excluding startup and warmup. The HTTP example's elapsed time also includes client transport and queueing. Neither is a device-kernel-only measurement.

Collect a profile separately to inspect attention, TopK, TensorMove, and small operators. Profile overhead changes latency; do not use trace collection runs as the unprofiled performance result. Identical measurement boundaries and inputs are required for a meaningful comparison.

For failures, retain a small relevant log window and use Troubleshooting. Remove credentials, private endpoints, and private paths before sharing diagnostics.

docs.title: Models and capabilities
docs.text: vLLM-GR has been validated with OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B. More models are being adapted and validated.

docs.title: Validated models
docs.text:
Model CUDA GPU Ascend NPU Get started OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B Validated Validated First inference

Model support is not tied to the 1.7B parameter count. Additional checkpoints require compatibility checks and validation before inclusion in this list.

Pangu is available as an additional NPU-specific workflow. See Pangu on NPU for the public checkpoint and SID preparation guide.

Choose a model and an inference path together. A checkpoint that generates text does not automatically contain recommendation SID tokens, a business catalog, or trained SID embeddings.

This guide describes the source snapshot used by this documentation edition, c4966f18. A supported code path is not a claim that every checkpoint, device, batch shape, or feature combination has passed hardware validation.

docs.title: Choose an entry point
docs.text:
Your goal Model and data Start here Run the standard recommendation example OneRec weights and tokenizer with the matching SID vocabulary; a compatible triples catalog First offline inference, then Online serving Generate ordinary text with public Pangu weights on NPU The public openPangu Embedded 1B checkpoint and its original tokenizer Pangu on NPU Exercise SID Beam execution using public Pangu assets on NPU A separately converted SID checkpoint and a matching synthetic catalog Pangu SID preparation workflow Search the full model vocabulary without a catalog A supported text decoder and an explicit unconstrained Beam configuration NPU unconstrained Beam guide; CUDA callers use the same public Beam API with the CUDA runtime Generate a thinking continuation before SID selection A checkpoint with the required thinking tokens and behavior, plus a compatible SID catalog Thinking and SID Beam example

The ordinary Pangu example uses GRLLM.generate(), which follows the standard vLLM generation path. The recommendation examples use GRLLM.beam_search_v1(). HTTP recommendation requests select Beam explicitly with use_beam_search: true; starting a server alone does not select that path.

The offline Python API and the HTTP service are separate frontends to the engine. An asynchronous engine does not require an HTTP server, and an offline GRLLM call can still use asynchronous scheduling internally. See the Beam execution contract for request ownership and lifecycle.

docs.title: Know which component owns what
docs.text:
Component Role What it does not supply Model configuration and weights Define the network, vocabulary dimensions, embeddings, and output projection used for inference A business item catalog or ground-truth evaluation dataset Tokenizer files Map text and SID symbols to token IDs and decode IDs back to text Trained vectors for newly added tokens Catalog or triples document Define which A/B/C SID combinations are legal recommendation candidates Learned probabilities or model training Compiled Constraint Table Turn catalog relations into an artifact for the selected backend, tied to its tokenizer identity A replacement for the model weights or tokenizer SID-to-item mapping Map complete generated SIDs to business item identifiers A guarantee that a randomly initialized SID model recommends useful items

Tokenizer assets are normally stored beside the weights in a model directory, but tokenization is outside the model's tensor forward computation. The token embedding and output projection are model tensors. Adding tokenizer entries without corresponding weight rows is not sufficient to extend a checkpoint.

A catalog can constrain a model to emit legal symbols even when the model has not learned useful preferences over those symbols. Legal output and useful recommendations therefore need different validation.

Use the same immutable local model/tokenizer snapshot when compiling the Constraint Table and running inference. A path name is not an identity check. The artifact and tokenizer digests in the canonical configuration identify the compiled inputs; changing the tokenizer or catalog requires rebuilding them. See Beam parameters and modes for the configuration fields and boundary-token budget. Follow Data and constraints to prepare reusable artifacts, or Python integration to embed the public Beam API in an application.

docs.title: Start with OneRec
docs.text:
The main walkthrough uses OpenOneRec/OneRec-1.7B, its tokenizer, the tracked video triples fixture, and a short prompt. It downloads weights separately from the framework and runs one request with capacity 128 and three generated SID components. Follow First offline inference without combining advanced options on the initial run.

The constrained example generates A, B, and C components. Its configured BEGIN and END positions are additional public-output positions, so max_tokens=5 represents three generated components. A one- or two-component run produces a valid catalog prefix; it is not a complete three-component item identifier.

The standalone example accepts a triples JSON document and compiles a temporary artifact. The online service instead loads a persistent artifact and canonical configuration. These inputs are not interchangeable command-line arguments.

For business use, replace the fixture with the catalog and SID-to-item mapping that belong to your model and task. Do not treat the example prompt, candidate legality, or one successful request as a Recall measurement. Use Validation and benchmarking for separate functional, numerical, recommendation-quality, and performance checks.

docs.title: Distinguish the two public Pangu workflows
Ordinary text generation
docs.text:
The NPU-specific Pangu guide provides the public checkpoint's text-generation path. This route does not require adding SID symbols or creating a recommendation catalog.

The Pangu compatibility layer preserves the checkpoint's declared tied embedding behavior. The public checkpoint can contain a zero-filled lm_head.weight placeholder; treating that placeholder as an independent output head would produce incorrect all-zero logits. This compatibility fix does not create a new Pangu architecture or train a recommendation model.

Use the Pangu-specific runtime settings from the example guide, including the slow tokenizer and its cache settings. Its NPU path selects KV block size 128. The ordinary text-generation settings are not a replacement for the canonical Beam configuration in the recommendation guides.

docs.title: SID execution with a converted checkpoint
docs.text:
At this source snapshot, the project's SID-extended Pangu checkpoint is not publicly available. The preparation tool makes execution smoke tests possible from public openpangu/openPangu-Embedded-1B-V1.1 assets.

Preparation reads a local public snapshot and writes a separate output directory. It refuses an existing destination and validates the result on CPU before publishing it. It expects the public Pangu architecture, original vocabulary size, tied embedding layout, and safetensors weights; it is not a generic converter for arbitrary Pangu checkpoints.

The conversion performs these operations:

  1. Preserve existing token IDs and original tokenizer entries, then add 8192 symbols in each of the A, B, and C SID families plus BEGIN and END markers.
  2. Expand the embedding tensor and initialize new SID and padding rows randomly using a fixed seed. Preserve the original embedding prefix and other model tensors.
  3. Materialize the tied output-head weights from the expanded embedding instead of retaining the public checkpoint's zero placeholder, and update vocabulary metadata.
  4. Write token-layout, tensor-inventory, and conversion-manifest reports with checksums and CPU validation results.

This changes tokenizer assets, vocabulary metadata, and embedding/output-head storage. It is not accurate to call the converted checkpoint byte-for-byte unchanged. It also does not train the new rows: their initialization supplies executable tensors, not learned recommendation knowledge.

The tool records a caller-declared source revision and hashes the local source files. Its manifest explicitly reports revision_verified: false; the revision label alone is not proof that local files came from that remote commit.

The documented smoke workflow builds a small synthetic catalog and uses the existing constrained Beam example on NPU. The catalog fixes legal A/B/C combinations, so successful output can look like valid SIDs despite random new weights. This establishes neither business accuracy nor a speedup. Preparation does not require an accelerator; the inference walkthrough requires the prepared Ascend runtime described in Pangu on NPU.

docs.title: Separate the Beam protocol from the model runner
docs.text:
beam.execution_mode: v1 and beam_search_v1() name the GR Beam protocol. They do not mean that every model forward must use native ModelRunner V1.

The runtime selection policy defaults to ModelRunner V1 before vLLM initialization. An explicit VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 is preserved as an experimental opt-in. The documented V2 adaptation targets CUDA; its runner guide records the workload, storage, capture, and lifecycle scope. Do not infer support for every V1 feature combination from that opt-in.

The NPU guides use ModelRunner V1. In particular, the NPU unconstrained adapter explicitly rejects ModelRunner V2. Switching runners does not bypass model, generation-budget, artifact, or parallelism validation.

docs.title: Check capabilities by execution path
docs.text:
The table below summarizes the default ModelRunner V1 Beam paths in this snapshot. It does not turn separate capabilities into a promise that all of them can be combined.

Capability CUDA Beam V1 path Ascend NPU Beam V1 path Three-component catalog-constrained generation Canonical CUDA table Canonical NPU table and required NPU operators Full-vocabulary Beam without catalog membership Explicit unconstrained configuration Explicit unconstrained configuration; effective budget remains 1 through 3 Dynamic retained widths and final result limit Python and HTTP interfaces Python, HTTP, and the standalone demo; keep scalar candidate width unset for changing widths Independent per-parent candidate schedules per_parent_beam_widths, subject to request and engine limits Not supported in this snapshot Multiple independent catalog Tries in one artifact Supported through per-request Trie selectors Multi-Trie artifacts and nonzero Trie selectors are rejected Catalog-free A/B/C stage domains Not the NPU stage-domain feature Opt-in beam.sid_stage_vocab, only with unconstrained generation Decode graph execution CUDA capture and replay policy Exact logical batch and Decode input-width capture, with separate fallback behavior

Constrained generation remains limited by the three-level table; increasing beam.max_decode_steps does not deepen the catalog. The current NPU unconstrained adapter also limits generation to 1 through 3 tokens. Ordinary LLM text generation is a different path and does not remove these Beam limits.

The multi-Trie contract uses one model vocabulary and tokenizer for all Tries. A request selector chooses a catalog root, not another model or another checkpoint. CPU table compilation/reference support does not establish a production CPU Beam inference engine.

In NPU catalog-free SID stage mode, selecting A/B/C families is not catalog membership checking. Stage-local probability normalization differs from full-vocabulary normalization and can change scores and cross-parent rankings. Compare implementations under the same probability domain. See the unconstrained scoring contract before enabling this mode.

For graph shapes and width rules, follow Beam parameters and modes. A graph-enabled setting is not evidence of actual replay, and replay is not a guarantee of numerical agreement for arbitrary padded Prefill inputs.

docs.title: Treat thinking as a separate model capability
docs.text:
The offline demo has two distinct optional routes: --enable-thinking performs ordinary full-vocabulary generation, while --cot generates a thinking continuation and then runs constrained SID Beam Search. They are mutually exclusive. Neither flag teaches reasoning to weights that do not support it.

The combined path requires dedicated <think> and </think> tokenizer tokens, a matching SID vocabulary/catalog, and enough context for both phases. It hands off token IDs and performs fresh Beam Prefill; it does not reuse thinking KV across phases. Its thinking budget does not extend the SID table's depth.

The source workflow documents the NPU setup and explicitly does not include CUDA hardware validation of the combined example. The shared script accepts both backends, which is different from proving equivalent quality, timing, or graph coverage on both. Qualify the chosen model, frontend, runner, and platform through validation.

Use Advanced Beam features for the current mode-specific walkthroughs and Configuration reference for engine keys.

docs.title: Online serving
docs.text:
Serve OneRec Beam Search through an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint on CUDA or Ascend NPU. This guide starts one local server and sends one prompt with Beam width 128 and three generated SID components.

Complete the platform installation or Ascend installation, then follow First offline inference to download the model and check the inference path. Run these commands from the vllm-gr repository root in the same accelerator environment. Stop the offline process before starting the server so it can use the device memory.

Already prepared an artifact and YAML with Data and constraints? Keep its MODEL, BACKEND, and WORKDIR in the server shell and continue at Start the server. The commands read $WORKDIR/vllm_gr_config.yaml; you do not need to rebuild the same artifact. The client terminal below uses its own output directory.

docs.title: 1. Set the paths and platform
docs.text:
Use the same local model snapshot and example constraint data as the offline guide. Set MODEL to your actual model directory if it differs:

export MODEL="$PWD/models/OneRec-1.7B"
export CATALOG="$PWD/tools/AB_Tests/constraints/video_constraint_triples.json"
export WORKDIR="$PWD/results/online-serving"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"
test -f "$MODEL/config.json"
test -f "$CATALOG"

Choose one backend, then run the common configuration step below:

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
export BACKEND=cuda

export BACKEND=npu

For NPU, keep the CANN and custom xllm-ops environments loaded in this shell, as described in the Ascend installation guide.

docs.title: 2. Build the artifact and server configuration
docs.text:
The service loads a persistent .safetensors Constraint Table. It does not accept the triples JSON as a server-side catalog argument. The following uses the repository's artifact builder and writes a canonical YAML configuration with the resulting absolute path and digests:

python - <<'PY'
import os
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
from tools.build_constraint_table import build_constraint_table
from vllm_gr.config import gr_config_from_mapping

backend = os.environ["BACKEND"]
if backend not in {"cuda", "npu"}:
    raise ValueError("BACKEND must be cuda or npu")
work = Path(os.environ["WORKDIR"]).resolve()
artifact = work / "video_constraint_table.safetensors"
artifact_digest, tokenizer_digest, _ = build_constraint_table(
    triples_path=os.environ["CATALOG"],
    model=str(Path(os.environ["MODEL"]).resolve()),
    revision=None,
    output_path=artifact,
    trust_remote_code=True,
)
config = {
    "schema_version": 1,
    "attention_backend": "CUSTOM",
    "beam": {
        "execution_mode": "v1",
        "graph_enabled": backend == "cuda",
        "graph_batch_size": 1,
        "online_batch_sizes": [1],
        "worker_decision": True,
        "max_width": 128,
        "max_decode_steps": 3,
    },
    "constraint_table": {
        "enabled": True,
        "backend": backend,
        "max_top_k": 128,
        "path": str(artifact),
        "format": "constraint_table_v1",
        "artifact_digest": artifact_digest,
        "tokenizer_digest": tokenizer_digest,
    },
}
gr_config_from_mapping(config)
config_path = work / "vllm_gr_config.yaml"
config_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(config, sort_keys=False), encoding="utf-8")
print(f"config={config_path}")
print(f"artifact_digest={artifact_digest}")
print(f"tokenizer_digest={tokenizer_digest}")
PY

Keep the artifact and YAML available at these paths while the server runs. Rebuild them when the constraint data or tokenizer changes. This preparation compiles the table; it does not run model inference. See Data and constraints for alternate catalog inputs and Python integration to load the same configuration without an HTTP server.

Configuration Purpose constraint_table.backend Match the accelerator running the server. path and the two digests Identify the artifact and the tokenizer used to compile it. beam.max_width: 128 Match the request's Beam width. beam.max_decode_steps: 3 Allocate the three-component SID generation budget. beam.online_batch_sizes: [1] Keep the initial example to one prompt per execution session. beam.graph_enabled Keep CUDA's graph path; start NPU in eager mode.

Do not add legacy flags such as --catalog-path, --beam-max-width, or a second attention-backend override alongside --vllm-gr-config.

docs.title: 3. Start the server
docs.text:
Run the command matching the backend used to generate the YAML. Leave this terminal running until you finish the client request.

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
vllm-gr serve "$MODEL" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --served-model-name onerec --trust-remote-code \
  --vllm-gr-config "$WORKDIR/vllm_gr_config.yaml" \
  --max-model-len 512 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-logprobs 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
  --async-scheduling --no-enable-chunked-prefill

vllm-gr serve "$MODEL" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --served-model-name onerec --trust-remote-code \
  --vllm-gr-config "$WORKDIR/vllm_gr_config.yaml" \
  --max-model-len 512 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-logprobs 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --block-size 128 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --async-scheduling --no-enable-chunked-prefill

The short prompt below fits the 512-token model and Prefill budgets. Keep asynchronous scheduling enabled and Chunked Prefill disabled for this V1 path. Startup can include model loading and compilation; wait for the server to be ready before sending requests.

NPU graph execution

The NPU example uses beam.graph_enabled: false and --enforce-eager. To try the NPU graph path later, set beam.graph_enabled: true in the YAML, remove --enforce-eager, and restart the server. Keep graph_batch_size: 1 for this single-prompt example. Graph execution and numerical parity are separate validation tasks.

docs.title: 4. Send a request
docs.text:
Open a second terminal on the same accelerator host, activate the client Python environment, and return to the repository root. Set these variables again; shell variables from the server terminal are not inherited:

export API=http://127.0.0.1:8000
export WORKDIR="$PWD/results/online-serving"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"

curl --fail --silent --show-error "$API/health"
curl --fail --silent --show-error "$API/v1/models" | python -m json.tool

/health should return HTTP 200, and /v1/models should list the configured name onerec. Write the request as JSON using Python, so prompt newlines and quotes are escaped correctly:

python - <<'PY'
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

request = {
    "model": "onerec",
    "prompt": (
        "Video history: <|sid_begin|><s_a_346><s_b_6566><s_c_5603><|sid_end|>.\n"
        "Recommend the next video."
    ),
    "use_beam_search": True,
    "stream": False,
    "n": 128,
    "temperature": 0.0,
    "max_tokens": 5,
    "ignore_eos": True,
    "skip_special_tokens": False,
    "include_stop_str_in_output": True,
    "vllm_xargs": {
        "begin_token": "<|sid_begin|>",
        "end_token": "<|sid_end|>",
    },
}
path = Path(os.environ["WORKDIR"]) / "request.json"
path.write_text(json.dumps(request, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
print(path)
PY

curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  "$API/v1/completions" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary "@$WORKDIR/request.json" \
  --output "$WORKDIR/response.json" \
  --write-out 'HTTP elapsed: %{time_total}s\n'

This uses the completions endpoint with a text prompt, without a chat template. The online path does not apply the offline demo's --input-len padding or truncation, so the two examples do not establish identical token shapes or latency.

Request field Meaning model: onerec Match --served-model-name, rather than the local directory name. use_beam_search: true Select Beam Search instead of ordinary sampling. n: 128 Set the Beam width to the server's configured width. It is not a display limit. max_tokens: 5 Reserve begin and end positions, leaving three generated SID components. The first component comes from Prefill, followed by two Decode steps. ignore_eos: true State V1's fixed-budget behavior. The online V1 entry supplies this value even if a client sends false. stream: false Receive one complete response with the final candidates. vllm_xargs Supply the SID begin and end tokens as Beam extensions.

docs.title: 5. Read the response
docs.text:
Inspect the returned count and the first five choices:

python - <<'PY'
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

path = Path(os.environ["WORKDIR"]) / "response.json"
response = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
if "error" in response:
    raise SystemExit(response["error"])
print(f"returned_choices={len(response['choices'])}")
for choice in response["choices"][:5]:
    print(choice["index"], choice["finish_reason"], choice["text"])
print("usage=", response.get("usage"))
PY

choices[].text contains the SID candidate text, index identifies the choice, and finish_reason describes completion. A length finish reason can be normal for this fixed-budget search; the output processor adds the configured end marker to surviving fixed-length candidates. The returned count can be below 128 when there are fewer valid candidates.

usage contains HTTP response token accounting. The offline example's sid_token_ids and cumulative_logprob JSON fields are not part of this HTTP response contract. This guide does not request per-token log probabilities.

The printed HTTP elapsed time is client-observed wall time, including HTTP overhead and any request queueing. It is not device kernel time or a steady-state benchmark. Use representative inputs and repeated controlled runs to measure latency and recommendation quality.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom What to check Connection refused Keep the server terminal running, wait for startup, and use the same host and port as the command. Model not found in the request Use model: onerec, matching the server alias; inspect /v1/models. Width validation error Keep request n equal to beam.max_width, both 128 here. Artifact, digest, or tokenizer mismatch Regenerate the artifact and YAML together from the same model snapshot and catalog. Engine initialization fails for memory Check the startup error and available device memory; avoid sharing a busy accelerator. Prompt does not fit the token budget This example uses 512 tokens. Increase the model and Prefill budgets together for longer complete prompts, within model and device limits. HTTP request fails Read response.json and the server log for the specific error; the curl command returns a nonzero status on HTTP errors.

This example intentionally uses a single prompt. The engine has a separate prompt-list batching policy; see the batching reference before enabling additional sizes. Full configuration details are in the online example.

Continue with Beam parameters and modes before adjusting widths, generation budgets, or graph shapes. See Validation and benchmarking for correctness checks and offline API latency measurements with an explicit timing boundary. For startup failures, HTTP errors, or artifact mismatches, use Troubleshooting. For prompt lists, capacity planning, and response-to-input mapping, continue with Serving and batching. Use Metrics and logging to interpret runtime evidence.

docs.title: Public Pangu on Ascend NPU
docs.text:
This guide covers openpangu/openPangu-Embedded-1B-V1.1 using the vLLM-GR source snapshot c4966f18. Pangu is an additional NPU workflow, separate from the main OneRec tutorial. It has two paths:

Workflow Input checkpoint Purpose Ordinary text inference Untouched public weights and tokenizer Run the repository's Pangu text-generation example and inspect its small arithmetic fixture. Constrained SID Beam smoke test A separate checkpoint prepared from those public assets Exercise SID tokenization, vocabulary rows, and the existing constrained Beam pipeline.

The SID workflow does not train recommendation behavior. Its new weight rows are random, and its catalog is synthetic. A legal SID is not evidence of business accuracy, useful rankings, or a performance improvement.

The converter expects this public checkpoint's architecture, original vocabulary, tied embeddings, and safetensors layout. Do not apply these steps to arbitrary Pangu models or an already extended checkpoint. See Models and capabilities for the component roles.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the platform and paths
docs.text:
Complete Ascend installation. Run these Bash commands from the vllm-gr source repository root, in the prepared vendor runtime's Python environment. Keep the CANN and custom xllm-ops environments loaded. Use an allocated NPU with sufficient free memory, and stop your own other inference workloads.

export PANGU_PUBLIC_REVISION=146d3a854e2930b5e3dfbf9dc1187a6c78f8decd
export PANGU_PUBLIC_MODEL_PATH="$PWD/models/openPangu-public-$PANGU_PUBLIC_REVISION"
export PANGU_SID_MODEL_PATH="$PWD/models/openPangu-public-sid-seed20261105"
export PANGU_WORKDIR="$PWD/results/pangu"
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
mkdir -p "$PANGU_WORKDIR/logs" "$PANGU_WORKDIR/json"
set -o pipefail

The public revision is the snapshot recorded by the conversion tool. Download it into the source directory; do not edit that directory or use it as the conversion output:

python - <<'PY' 2>&1 | tee "$PANGU_WORKDIR/logs/download.log"
import os
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

path = snapshot_download(
    repo_id="openpangu/openPangu-Embedded-1B-V1.1",
    revision=os.environ["PANGU_PUBLIC_REVISION"],
    local_dir=os.environ["PANGU_PUBLIC_MODEL_PATH"],
)
print(f"model={path}")
print(f"revision={os.environ['PANGU_PUBLIC_REVISION']}")
PY

Keep weights, configuration, tokenizer, and any model-provided code from the same snapshot. Model downloads require network access and enough disk space; see the Hugging Face download guide for authentication and cache options. Reuse a local copy only if it is the untouched matching snapshot.

docs.title: 2. Run ordinary text inference
docs.text:
The Pangu example uses GRLLM.generate() and ordinary sampling parameters. It does not enable SID Beam or need a Constraint Table. The source selects BF16, the slow tokenizer, and disables Chunked Prefill and Prefix Cache; its NPU path uses KV block size 128. This ordinary text path is not the width-32, three-step SID Beam path used later in this guide.

These commands use the checked-in eight-question arithmetic fixture. A smaller context limit is sufficient for this example; it is not the model's advertised maximum context length:

PANGU1B_MAX_MODEL_LEN=2048 \
python -u examples/offline_inference/pangu1b/pangu_generate.py \
  --model "$PANGU_PUBLIC_MODEL_PATH" \
  --dataset-path tests/resources/pangu1b/gsm8k_mini.json \
  --num-prompts 8 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0.0 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
  --block-size 128 --min-accuracy 0.5 \
  --output-json "$PANGU_WORKDIR/json/text-npu.json" \
  2>&1 | tee "$PANGU_WORKDIR/logs/text-npu.log"

The script prints accuracy, correct, num_samples, and elapsed_time, and saves generated answers and extraction details in the requested JSON. The explicit 0.5 is this example script's default threshold, not the CI policy. A nonzero exit when the threshold is missed is an evaluation failure, which is different from an engine startup error; inspect the saved details.

The arithmetic score is neither recommendation Recall nor a broad reasoning benchmark. elapsed_time includes engine construction and generation; it is not a steady-state request-latency measurement. The compatibility layer preserves the public checkpoint's tied embedding behavior instead of treating its zero output-head placeholder as an independent learned head.

For ordinary Pangu HTTP text serving, use the source example. Do not attach the OneRec constrained service configuration to ordinary text generation. The remainder of this page creates a different checkpoint for SID execution only.

docs.title: 3. Prepare a separate untrained SID checkpoint
docs.text:
At this source snapshot, the project's SID-extended Pangu checkpoint is not publicly available. The conversion tool provides a reproducible execution fixture using public weights, without introducing a new Pangu network implementation.

Preparation runs on CPU and requires torch, safetensors, transformers, sentencepiece, and protobuf. huggingface_hub is needed for the download. An installed vLLM-GR accelerator environment already supplies its compatible Torch and Transformers stack; keep those wheels, especially the Ascend vendor packages. If helper packages are missing, install only the missing helpers:

python -m pip install sentencepiece protobuf huggingface_hub

CPU preparation can instead run in a separate isolated environment containing those dependencies; it needs no accelerator or installed vLLM-GR. Install any CPU Torch wheel only in that separate environment, then return to the matching accelerator environment for inference. Do not replace vendor Torch/torch-npu merely to run this preparation tool.

The destination must not already exist and must be separate from the source. Do not create PANGU_SID_MODEL_PATH with mkdir. To prepare a different run, choose a new output directory rather than overwriting a checkpoint:

python -u tools/model_conversion/prepare_pangu_sid.py \
  --source "$PANGU_PUBLIC_MODEL_PATH" \
  --source-revision "$PANGU_PUBLIC_REVISION" \
  --output "$PANGU_SID_MODEL_PATH" \
  --seed 20261105 \
  2>&1 | tee "$PANGU_WORKDIR/logs/conversion.log"

The tool stages the output and publishes its directory after CPU validation. Its completion status is converted_and_cpu_validated; this is not an accelerator inference test. The prepared checkpoint contains:

  • Existing token IDs and original embedding rows, with other model tensors preserved.
  • 8192 symbols per A, B, and C family plus SID BEGIN/END markers; new embedding and padding rows are initialized randomly using the fixed seed.
  • A tied lm_head.weight materialized from the expanded embedding, replacing the public zero placeholder, plus updated vocabulary metadata.
  • sid_token_ids.json, conversion_tensor_inventory.json, and conversion_manifest.json for token layout, checksums, and validation results.

This changes tokenizer assets and weight storage. Preserving the original embedding prefix does not make the full checkpoint unchanged or guarantee identical ordinary text output after vocabulary expansion. No training has taught the random rows a relationship to real items.

--source-revision is a declaration. The manifest hashes the actual local files but reports revision_verified: false; it does not authenticate those files against the remote revision. Keep converted weights and local conversion reports outside source control.

docs.title: 4. Build a synthetic catalog and triples
docs.text:
The catalog below contains every combination of eight A, eight B, and eight C symbols: 512 complete triples. It is a functional fixture with enough final paths for Beam width 32, not a business item mapping or evaluation dataset.

python - <<'PY'
import itertools
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

work = Path(os.environ["PANGU_WORKDIR"]) / "sid-inputs"
work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
catalog = [
    ["<|sid_begin|>", f"<s_a_{a}>", f"<s_b_{b}>", f"<s_c_{c}>", "<|sid_end|>"]
    for a, b, c in itertools.product(range(8), repeat=3)
]
(work / "catalog.json").write_text(json.dumps(catalog, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
(work / "prompt.txt").write_text("Return a semantic ID for this request.\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"catalog_entries={len(catalog)}")
PY

python tools/build_constraint_triples.py \
  --catalog "$PANGU_WORKDIR/sid-inputs/catalog.json" \
  --output "$PANGU_WORKDIR/sid-inputs/constraint_triples.json" \
  --begin '<|sid_begin|>' --end '<|sid_end|>' \
  2>&1 | tee "$PANGU_WORKDIR/logs/build-triples.log"

Pass the resulting triples document to the Beam demo, not the raw list in catalog.json. Every symbol must be present in the prepared tokenizer; do not substitute an unrelated public model directory. See Data and constraints for artifact identities and the separate persistent-artifact route used by applications and services.

docs.title: 5. Run constrained SID Beam
docs.text:
Return to the installed Ascend environment if preparation used a separate CPU environment. Retain the exported paths and custom operator environment in this shell:

python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$PANGU_SID_MODEL_PATH" \
  --catalog "$PANGU_WORKDIR/sid-inputs/constraint_triples.json" \
  --prompt "$PANGU_WORKDIR/sid-inputs/prompt.txt" \
  --constraint-backend npu --execution eager \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 32 --generated-steps 3 \
  --input-len 128 --max-model-len 2048 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --print-beams 5 \
  2>&1 | tee "$PANGU_WORKDIR/logs/sid-npu.log"

The demo compiles a temporary Constraint Table, sets the engine and request widths consistently, and prints returned candidates. Its three generated SID components use public max_tokens=5 with BEGIN/END positions. The first component comes from Prefill; two Decode steps produce the remaining two.

--input-len 128 prepares 127 prompt tokens plus the appended BEGIN position, using truncation or newline padding. This is a fixed-shape execution fixture, not evidence of unchanged prompt semantics or realistic recommendation quality. The SID command requests NPU eager execution. It does not establish graph replay or a performance comparison with the ordinary text workflow.

The constrained table determines legal A/B/C combinations. Random SID weights determine their scores and ordering within that legal set, so valid-looking SIDs are expected and are not proof that the checkpoint learned recommendation. Inspect candidate IDs, boundary tokens, and the generated catalog together.

This page documents the checked-in workflow; it does not report a new hardware qualification of these commands. Use Validation and benchmarking for device execution, numerical agreement, graph replay, and quality evidence. For an application integration after preparing a suitable persistent artifact, see Python integration. Do not copy its OneRec capacity 128 configuration unchanged into this width-32 fixture.

docs.title: Beam parameters and modes
docs.text:
Use this reference after First offline inference or Online serving. Start with one prompt, capacity 128, three SID components, and the matching platform configuration, then change one setting at a time.

This page describes the vLLM-GR 0.30 source used by these guides. A field being accepted by the configuration parser does not mean every accelerator supports every combination. Device-specific limits are called out below. For the selection and KV flow, read Beam Search explained. Use Models and capabilities to choose an entry point before configuring its parameters. For canonical field defaults, see Configuration reference. For mode-specific workflows, use Advanced Beam features.

docs.title: Capacity, candidates, retained width, and results
docs.text:
These four quantities serve different purposes:

Quantity Meaning Capacity W Engine storage and request capacity, configured by beam.max_width. Request beam_width must equal it. Candidates K How many token candidates each parent Beam can contribute before global selection. Retained width w_t How many winning prefixes survive after generated component t. A dynamic schedule sets one value per component. Result limit R Maximum final sequences returned to the caller. It does not reduce earlier search widths.

At each stage, candidate children compete globally to fill the retained width. One parent can contribute several winners, and another can contribute none. Limiting candidates per parent does not guarantee that every parent survives. The selected children carry their parent indices into KV inheritance and reordering, so each next-step prefix reads the history of its selected parent.

In the fixed-width default, w_t = W and the candidate count follows that width. For a dynamic schedule with candidate width left unset, candidate selection follows the current stage's retained width. An explicitly configured scalar candidate_width fixes the candidate count instead, unless a supported per-stage per-parent schedule overrides it. Check the platform limits below.

Reducing result_width limits the final returned set. Reducing --print-beams only prints fewer records in the offline demo. Neither option is a substitute for narrowing the search schedule.

docs.title: Engine startup configuration
docs.text:
Change these in the YAML passed to --vllm-gr-config, or in the Python vllm_gr_config mapping, before constructing the engine:

Setting Rule beam.execution_mode Use v1 for beam_search_v1(). beam.max_width Match every request's beam_width or HTTP n. The guides use 128. beam.max_decode_steps Must cover the effective generation budget, including the first component produced by Prefill. beam.worker_decision Keep true for the V1 path. constraint_table.candidate_width Optional engine-wide scalar K; leave unset for the NPU examples here. constraint_table.max_top_k Candidate storage limit; must cover the candidate counts required by the chosen execution path. beam.graph_enabled Enable the Beam Decode graph path; this is separate from Prefill graph controls. beam.graph_batch_size Exact NPU logical batch size for Beam Decode graph replay. beam.graph_widths Additional exact NPU Decode input widths to capture. beam.online_batch_sizes Policy for supported HTTP prompt-list batch sizes, not the request's Beam width. The online guide starts with [1].

The artifact path, artifact digest, tokenizer digest, and device backend must describe the same model/tokenizer and constraint table. Do not mix canonical configuration with legacy catalog or Beam CLI overrides.

docs.title: Per-request parameters
docs.text:
Python uses vllm_gr.sampling_params.BeamSearchParams. HTTP uses the fields below with use_beam_search: true:

Python field HTTP field Rule beam_width n Must equal engine beam.max_width, even with a dynamic schedule. max_tokens max_tokens Public generation budget, including configured begin/end positions. begin_token, end_token Inside vllm_xargs Use boundary tokens present in the checkpoint's tokenizer. dynamic_beam_widths vllm_xargs.dynamic_beam_widths One retained width per effective generation step, each between 1 and capacity. result_width vllm_xargs.result_width Between 1 and the final retained width; defaults to that final width. per_parent_beam_widths vllm_xargs.per_parent_beam_widths Per-stage candidate counts; currently CUDA-only. ignore_eos ignore_eos V1 uses a fixed budget. Set true in Python; the online entry supplies true itself. length_penalty length_penalty Final ranking control, separate from search capacity and candidate count.

For the canonical Constraint Table path, leave catalog_strategy unset. The Worker-side table controls candidate validity.

docs.title: Offline demo arguments
docs.text:
The standalone offline_beam_search_v1.py builds the engine configuration as well as the request. Its argument names are not identical to the Python API:

CLI argument Effect --beam-width Sets both engine capacity and request width. --generated-steps Effective SID steps, with choices 1, 2, or 3. --candidate-width Sets the engine's scalar candidate count; it is not the thinking sampler's --top-k. --dynamic-beam-widths Per-stage retained widths; this demo currently exposes this option only for NPU. --result-width Final return limit; this demo currently exposes this option only for NPU. --execution eager/graph NPU execution selection; it does not switch CUDA to eager mode. --input-len Prepares a fixed-length prompt for direct SID Beam, including the appended begin token. --print-beams Display limit for the returned records.

In direct SID Beam mode, the script sets public max_tokens to --generated-steps + 2 and Beam temperature to 0.0. Its --max-tokens, --temperature, --top-p, and --top-k arguments control thinking generation, not direct SID Beam selection. There is no demo CLI flag for per_parent_beam_widths; use the Python or HTTP interface on CUDA.

docs.title: Count generation steps correctly
docs.text:
The effective generation budget is:

N = max_tokens - configured_begin_position - configured_end_position

Each configured boundary reserves one position. With both OneRec markers, max_tokens=5 means N=3: Prefill selects A, then two Decode forwards select B and C. A surviving fixed-length result receives its configured end marker during output conversion; the marker is not another sampled Decode step.

The constraint_table_v1 path supports effective budgets 1 through 3. Use three components for the complete A/B/C SID example. A one-step run finishes in Prefill and should not be expected to report a Decode graph replay.

Increasing beam.max_decode_steps alone does not extend the constraint table's depth. The current NPU full-vocabulary Beam path also supports only 1 through 3 steps; do not infer longer-step support from ordinary LLM generation.

docs.title: Dynamic narrowing and widening
docs.text:
Keep engine and request capacity at 128. Both of these schedules fit within that capacity:

Schedule After Prefill: A After Decode 1: B After Decode 2: C Example return limit Narrowing 128 64 32 16 Widening 32 64 128 16

Each value is a retained prefix count, not a new engine capacity. Expanding a later stage creates more children of the surviving parents; it cannot recover prefixes already pruned at an earlier stage. Different schedules can change rankings and recommendation quality.

The examples below reuse the exported MODEL, CATALOG, and PROMPT paths from First offline inference. They leave scalar candidate_width unset and use the NPU demo's graph configuration:

NarrowingWidening 
python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" --catalog "$CATALOG" --prompt "$PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend npu --execution graph \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 \
  --input-len 128 --generated-steps 3 \
  --dynamic-beam-widths 128,64,32 --result-width 16 \
  --print-beams 5

python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" --catalog "$CATALOG" --prompt "$PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend npu --execution graph \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 \
  --input-len 128 --generated-steps 3 \
  --dynamic-beam-widths 32,64,128 --result-width 16 \
  --print-beams 5

Python and HTTP support retained-width schedules on CUDA as well as NPU. The demo's NPU-only CLI restriction is not a CUDA engine limitation.

docs.title: Match NPU graph shapes to Decode inputs
docs.text:
A three-component schedule has only two Decode input widths:

Retained schedule Decode input widths Suggested beam.graph_widths [128, 64, 32] 128, then 64 [64, 128] [32, 64, 128] 32, then 64 [32, 64]

The last retained width has no following model forward. NPU graph matching uses logical batch size and input width together, so a B=1 capture does not establish B=4 replay. The maximum-capacity width is included implicitly; the configuration allows at most eight distinct width captures including it. More captures increase startup and device-memory requirements.

The offline demo derives its graph widths from the schedule. When editing an online configuration yourself, set the matching graph_batch_size and graph_widths before restarting. For NPU graph execution, also set graph_enabled: true and remove --enforce-eager, as shown in Online serving.

A graph fallback counter means the Beam FULL graph was not used; it does not exclusively count eager forwards. Prefill capture has separate controls and shape restrictions. Use execution diagnostics or profiles to establish what actually replayed, and validate numerical behavior separately.

docs.title: Candidate-width and platform limits
docs.text:
On CUDA, per_parent_beam_widths sets one candidate count per effective step. The first must equal the first retained width. At each later step, the retained width cannot exceed the previous retained width times the per-parent candidate count. These are candidate limits, not a guarantee of one winner per parent.

The configuration schema has a global capacity ceiling of 1024 and candidate ceiling of 256. Capacity above 256 requires an explicitly configured candidate width at or below 256. These numeric ceilings are not a claim that every NPU shape or CUDA workload has been validated on hardware.

Feature CUDA V1 NPU V1 in this source version Three-component catalog-constrained Beam Supported Supported Dynamic retained widths and final result limit Python/HTTP interfaces Python/HTTP and the standalone demo Independent scalar candidate count Supported within the configured limits Keep unset; the NPU path requires candidate and retained widths to agree. Per-stage per_parent_beam_widths Supported within request and engine limits Not supported Multi-Trie request selection Separate CUDA configuration Not supported

An explicit scalar candidate_width must fit the candidate storage and max_logprobs budget. For a dynamic retained-width schedule without a per-stage candidate override, it must be at least every retained width. On NPU, leave it unset for changing retained widths; setting a fixed candidate count is not a way to enable independent candidate selection there.

docs.title: Choose the generation mode
docs.text:
Mode What it generates How to select it Catalog-constrained SID Beam Prefixes that follow the supplied catalog table Use the enabled canonical Constraint Table in the offline/online guides. Full-vocabulary Beam Model-vocabulary tokens, without catalog membership guarantees Use the public Python Beam API with constrained_generation: false and a disabled table. Catalog-free SID stage domains A, then B, then C token families, without validating the combined item On NPU, add beam.sid_stage_vocab: true to the unconstrained configuration. Thinking only Ordinary LLM generation, without a SID Beam phase The demo's --enable-thinking mode. Thinking followed by SID Beam A thinking continuation, then constrained SID search The demo's --cot mode and a compatible model/tokenizer/catalog.

--cot and --enable-thinking are mutually exclusive. Their thinking budget and sampler settings are separate from the SID Beam budget. A model must support the intended thinking behavior; selecting a mode does not add that capability to arbitrary weights.

The current NPU unconstrained path uses ModelRunner V1, FP16/BF16, asynchronous scheduling, and single-device parallelism. The SID stage domain is limited to three components. See the NPU unconstrained Beam guide for its complete configuration and scoring contract.

For the source behind this reference, see request parameters, configuration definitions, and the standalone demo.

docs.title: Python integration
docs.text:
Embed one constrained OneRec Beam request in a Python application without starting an HTTP server. This example reuses a persistent artifact and canonical YAML from Online serving or Data and constraints. It uses one prompt, capacity 128, and three generated SID components on the selected accelerator.

Run from the source repository root in the installed CUDA or Ascend environment. Stop your own server before starting this separate engine so both processes do not compete for the device memory. Keep the model/tokenizer snapshot and artifact unchanged between preparation and inference.

docs.title: Choose the application interface
docs.text:
Interface Application behavior Execution relationship GRLLM.beam_search_v1() A synchronous Python call returns final Beam outputs The engine still uses asynchronous scheduling internally. Async engine with GR adapters An event-loop application manages asynchronous submission, result delivery, and cleanup This does not inherently require HTTP; see the source pointers below. OpenAI-compatible HTTP service A client sends requests to a separately running server The server uses the asynchronous engine and GR frontend adaptation.

Calling GRLLM directly does not make the application an AsyncLLM client. Conversely, asynchronous inference is not restricted to an HTTP deployment. The public beam_search_v1 name identifies the Beam protocol, separately from the native model runner. The example below keeps ModelRunner V1.

docs.title: Reuse the prepared configuration
docs.text:
Use the same backend that you selected when generating the YAML. If it differs, regenerate the configuration through the preparation guide rather than changing only an environment variable.

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
export BACKEND=cuda

export BACKEND=npu

Set the paths again in this shell. This uses the output directory from artifact and configuration preparation. If you reused the online guide instead, set WORKDIR to "$PWD/results/online-serving". Replace MODEL if needed. PROMPT refers to the short text file from the offline guide, not its length-padded token sequence:

export MODEL="$PWD/models/OneRec-1.7B"
export WORKDIR="$PWD/results/data-preparation"
export GR_CONFIG="$WORKDIR/vllm_gr_config.yaml"
export PROMPT="$PWD/results/first-inference/prompt.txt"
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
test -f "$MODEL/config.json"
test -f "$GR_CONFIG"
test -f "$PROMPT"

Select an available device through your environment's allocation process. On NPU, retain the CANN and xllm-ops environments described by Ascend installation. Environment variables select inputs and visibility; they do not create the corresponding runtime or artifacts.

The configuration loader is the public vllm_gr.config.load_gr_config() function. It returns a validated GRConfig and resolves relative artifact paths against the YAML's directory. GRLLM accepts that object, a canonical mapping, or a YAML path through vllm_gr_config. A mapping with relative paths does not automatically inherit the directory of some separately loaded YAML.

docs.title: Run a complete synchronous example
docs.text:
Save the following program as python_beam.py under $WORKDIR. Using a real file and a __main__ guard lets spawned engine processes import the main module safely; do not replace the launch with Python executing from standard input when using the spawn process model.

python_beam.py
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path


def main():
    from vllm.inputs import tokens_input
    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
    from vllm_gr.config import BeamExecutionMode, load_gr_config, resolve_candidate_width
    from vllm_gr.entrypoints.gr import GRLLM
    from vllm_gr.sampling_params import BeamSearchParams

    backend = os.environ["BACKEND"]
    if backend not in {"cuda", "npu"}:
        raise ValueError("BACKEND must be cuda or npu")
    if str(current_platform.device_type) != backend:
        raise ValueError("BACKEND does not match the active accelerator runtime")
    model = Path(os.environ["MODEL"]).resolve()
    config = load_gr_config(os.environ["GR_CONFIG"])
    table = config.constraint_table
    if table is None or not table.enabled or table.backend.value != backend:
        raise ValueError("Use an enabled table configuration matching BACKEND")
    if config.beam_execution_mode is not BeamExecutionMode.V1:
        raise ValueError("The configuration must select beam.execution_mode=v1")
    if config.beam_max_width != 128 or config.beam_max_decode_steps < 3:
        raise ValueError("This example requires capacity 128 and at least 3 SID steps")
    if config.beam_worker_decision is not True:
        raise ValueError("Keep beam.worker_decision=true")
    if config.beam_graph_enabled != (backend == "cuda"):
        raise ValueError("Use the guide's CUDA graph or NPU eager configuration")
    candidate_width = resolve_candidate_width(config)
    if candidate_width != 128 or table.max_top_k < candidate_width:
        raise ValueError("Reuse the guide's candidate capacity of 128")

    params = BeamSearchParams(
        beam_width=128,
        max_tokens=5,
        temperature=0.0,
        ignore_eos=True,
        begin_token="<|sid_begin|>",
        end_token="<|sid_end|>",
        include_stop_str_in_output=True,
        length_penalty=1.0,
    )
    device_kwargs = {"block_size": 128} if backend == "npu" else {}
    with GRLLM(
        model=str(model),
        trust_remote_code=True,
        vllm_gr_config=config,
        async_scheduling=True,
        enable_prefix_caching=True,
        enable_chunked_prefill=False,
        max_model_len=512,
        max_num_batched_tokens=512,
        max_num_seqs=128,
        max_logprobs=candidate_width,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
        enforce_eager=backend == "npu",
        **device_kwargs,
    ) as llm:
        tokenizer = llm.get_tokenizer()
        text = Path(os.environ["PROMPT"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        prompt_ids = tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
        if not prompt_ids or len(prompt_ids) + params.max_tokens > 512:
            raise ValueError("Use a nonempty prompt fitting the full public token budget")
        print(f"input_tokens={len(prompt_ids)}; the API appends BEGIN")
        outputs = llm.beam_search_v1(
            [tokens_input(prompt_ids)], params, output_mode="compact"
        )
        for request_index, output in enumerate(outputs):
            print(f"request={request_index} returned_beams={len(output.sequences)}")
            for rank, sequence in enumerate(output.sequences[:5]):
                ids = list(sequence.token_ids)
                print(json.dumps({
                    "request": request_index,
                    "rank": rank,
                    "token_ids": ids,
                    "text": tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=False),
                    "cumulative_logprob": sequence.cumulative_logprob,
                    "finish_reason": sequence.finish_reason,
                    "stop_reason": sequence.stop_reason,
                }, ensure_ascii=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run the saved file from the same shell:

python -u "$WORKDIR/python_beam.py"

The YAML owns GR engine choices and artifact identity. Native engine options such as memory utilization and scheduling stay on the constructor. Request boundaries and the generation budget belong to BeamSearchParams. Do not add legacy catalog/Beam constructor overrides alongside the canonical configuration, or pass platform switches such as enable_npugraph_ex as arbitrary top-level GRLLM keywords. See Troubleshooting.

This example encodes the complete file without padding or truncation. It conservatively reserves the full public five-position budget inside the 512-token limit. Do not append an extra BEGIN marker yourself: the API adds it before Prefill. Three SID components then require Prefill and two Decode forwards. The END marker is handled during completion/output conversion.

The NPU example uses both beam.graph_enabled: false in its YAML and enforce_eager=True on the constructor. The CUDA example keeps the guide's graph-enabled configuration. Configured graph behavior is not evidence that all Prefill or Decode shapes actually replayed. Validate graph execution and numerical agreement separately before changing these settings.

docs.title: Read the output format explicitly
docs.text:
compact is the default output mode; this example selects it explicitly. Its result records hold ordinary CPU token IDs and scores:

Output Fields and contents One request result sequences plus one shared prompt_token_ids value containing the accepted original input. One compact candidate token_ids, cumulative_logprob, finish_reason, and stop_reason. Compact token_ids Generated suffix only, including configured BEGIN/END markers; the original prompt is excluded. Candidate text Decode its token IDs explicitly with the same tokenizer, as the script does.

There can be fewer valid candidates than capacity 128. Printing five records does not reduce the search width. Scores are the search's cumulative log probabilities, not a normalized probability distribution over returned items. This functional example establishes no recommendation-quality or latency claim.

The explicit alternative output_mode="full" returns native-style lazy Beam sequences. Their fields are tokens and cum_logprob, rather than compact token_ids and cumulative_logprob. Full tokens include the original prompt; reading full tokens/text can perform deferred CPU materialization. Do not change only the mode while keeping the compact-format field accesses above.

Keep one engine alive for the requests your application owns instead of loading a model for every candidate. The context manager calls shutdown() on exit, including when the body raises an exception. It is separate from the per-call Beam session's release lifecycle. Stop using the engine after leaving the context; do not replace shutdown with termination of unrelated device processes.

docs.title: Async applications and HTTP
docs.text:
This source snapshot does not export a GRAsyncLLM convenience class. It does contain an asynchronous Beam control flow, an async client adapter, and extensions to native AsyncLLM. These components can support an embedded asynchronous application without an HTTP transport. The engine-only adapter expects prepared Beam requests; it is not a drop-in await GRLLM.beam_search_v1() interface.

Direct async integration must own input preparation, session submission, terminal result delivery, cancellation, release, and engine shutdown. This page does not turn those internal building blocks into an unverified public wrapper. For the supported request/response service workflow, follow Online serving; for a custom async frontend, begin with the lifecycle contract and the pinned implementations above.

Use Python API reference for public fields and Advanced Beam features before changing the generation mode.

docs.title: Installation for Ascend NPU
docs.text: For the complete path from installation to your first request, start with Quickstart. This page prepares the Ascend NPU environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An Ascend NPU host (verified on 910B) with the matching driver
  • A container runtime (Docker or Podman)
  • The vendor image quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0rc2
  • 32GB+ RAM (recommended)

The vendor image already contains the complete validated runtime: Python 3.12, CANN 9.2.0, PyTorch / torch-npu 2.10.0, Triton-Ascend 3.6.0, vLLM 0.30.0, vLLM-Ascend 0.30.0rc2, and the matching numpy / cv2 pair. No part of that stack is installed by hand.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/JiusiServe/vllm-gr.git
cd vllm-gr
  1. Enter the validated base environment

Run all remaining steps inside a container based on the vendor image quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0rc2. That image is the validated base environment of this vllm-gr release: it supplies the complete vendor stack (vLLM 0.30.0, vLLM-Ascend 0.30.0rc2, Triton-Ascend 3.6.0, torch / torch-npu 2.10.0, CANN 9.2.0) together with the matching numpy and cv2 pair, and the NPU runtime validation of this release was performed inside it.

This vllm-gr release supports the vLLM 0.30.0 API only.

vllm_gr._env_check pins the validated vendor pair (vLLM-Ascend 0.30.0rc2 with Triton-Ascend 3.6.0) and rejects a mismatched runtime at startup, so a different vllm-ascend release fails fast instead of serving.

Installing the vendor stack with plain pip is not a supported alternative:

  • Triton-Ascend is not published on PyPI.
  • The torch build used by the image has no public PyPI distribution.
  • The image's opencv distribution declares numpy>=2, while its triton-ascend distribution declares numpy==1.26.4; those particular metadata requirements cannot both be satisfied by a pip resolver.

See the vllm-ascend v0.30.0rc2 installation reference.

  1. Install xllm-ops
# Clone the xllm-ops repository
git clone https://github.com/xLLM-AI/xllm-ops.git

# Prepare the xllm-ops build
cd xllm-ops
git submodule init
git submodule update

# Load the CANN environment supplied by the base image
source "${ASCEND_TOOLKIT_HOME}/set_env.sh"

# Build the operator subset vllm-gr calls. CANN 9.2.0's op store ships a
# built-in CausalConv1d that collides with xllm-ops' custom operator of the
# same type name, so build only the required operators instead of the full
# set; the --no-build-* flags skip the unrelated third-party operator
# libraries.
bash build.sh -c ascend910b \
  -n "beam_search_group;cache_unshared_kv;select_unshared_kv;x_attention;onerec_final_beam_select;rec_constrained_top_k" \
  --no-build-transformer --no-build-flash

# Load the freshly installed custom operator library
source "${ASCEND_HOME_PATH}/opp/vendors/custom_xllm_math/bin/set_env.bash"

# Install the xllm-ops library
cd test/python_test
bash build_and_run.sh

Return to the vllm-gr directory before continuing.

  1. Install vllm-gr
VLLM_GR_TARGET_DEVICE=npu pip install -e . --no-build-isolation

For developer mode:

VLLM_GR_TARGET_DEVICE=npu pip install -e ".[dev]" --no-build-isolation

requirements/npu.txt installs the shared dependencies only; the vendor runtime comes from the base image. Confirm that the complete Ascend runtime pair was resolved correctly:

python -c 'import importlib.metadata as m; print("vllm", m.version("vllm")); print("vllm-ascend", m.version("vllm-ascend")); print("vllm-gr", m.version("vllm-gr"))'
  1. Verify installation
python -c "import vllm_gr; print(vllm_gr.__version__)"
python -c "from vllm_gr._env_check import check_environment; print(check_environment())"
python -c "import numpy, cv2; print('numpy', numpy.__version__, 'cv2', cv2.__version__)"

docs.title: Jenkins test runtime
docs.text:
tools/run_test.sh checks the active NPU Python against the versions declared by the checkout before running resource tests, selecting a device or loading custom operators. The check uses tools/ci/resolve_runtime.py, as the GitHub Actions runtime setup does. It reports the required and installed versions and fails when they disagree.

An older Jenkins job or Conda environment named vllm-gr-0.22 or xGr-install-22 does not become a 0.30 runtime after installing this repository. The NPU extra intentionally leaves the vendor stack to the base environment. Run the job inside the validated vendor image described above, and ensure CONDA_PREFIX, PATH and the CANN environment all select that same runtime. Do not copy an old CANN custom-operator build into the new image; rebuild it for the image's CANN version.

Before installing GR or launching the gate, the selected Python can check the base environment without importing vLLM or allocating an NPU:

python3 tools/ci/resolve_runtime.py resolve --device npu \
  --output /tmp/vllm-gr-npu-runtime.json
VLLM_GR_TARGET_DEVICE=npu python3 -m pip install -e ".[dev]" --no-build-isolation
bash tools/run_test.sh

GPU-only attention tests skip on the NPU target before importing CUDA-only vLLM APIs. That device boundary does not make an older vendor runtime compatible; the runtime check remains required.

docs.title: Vendor package metadata
docs.text:
Keep the output of python -m pip check as an environment diagnostic. The validated image has known metadata conflicts, so that command alone cannot establish whether this vendor runtime works. Recorded reports include:

  • Declaration conflict: the image's opencv-python-headless 5.x wheel declares numpy>=2 while triton-ascend 3.6.0 declares numpy==1.26.4. The successful runtime validation used the vendor-supplied cv2 build. Confirm its actual import with NumPy 1.26.4; a version declaration or vLLM's lazy import fallback is not evidence of binary compatibility.
  • Metadata drift: the image's vllm-ascend metadata declares slightly older companions (triton-ascend 3.2.2, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4) than the image actually ships (3.6.0, post7).

Treat these recorded vendor-image discrepancies separately from new missing or incompatible dependencies. Validate runtime versions, direct numpy/cv2 imports, custom operator loading, and inference inside the selected image. Do not ignore unrelated pip check errors or replace vendor packages merely to silence the known reports. Package availability on PyPI and consistency of installed package metadata are separate questions.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Continue with First offline inference to prepare OneRec weights and run a constrained Beam request on NPU.

After installation, use the online V1 serving guide with constraint_table.backend: npu and the NPU execution settings below.

docs.title: NPU decode execution options
docs.text:
Beam Search V1 uses a fixed request width equal to beam.max_width (vllm_gr_beam_max_width in the legacy configuration encoding). A smaller request width is rejected before submission; the NPU batch pool is not a variable-width view. Native request state advances by one token per request at Decode, while the NPU model executes batch_size * beam_width tokens.

The incremental beam decode branch on Ascend NPU has two execution modes, selected through the engine's additional_config:

  • xllm (default when the xllm-ops library is installed): the fused path — a single x_attention kernel attends over the paged shared prefix and the contiguous unshared beam pool at once, and the fused cache_unshared_kv / select_unshared_kv operators handle pool writes and beam-selection reorders.
  • cascade: the per-operator path — two npu_fused_infer_attention_score_v2 calls plus the pool-to-buffer copies and the merge operator chain. This is the default on NPU when xllm-ops is missing (a log line explains why) and always the default on CUDA.

These additional_config examples select the attention adapter and the NPU decode execution mode only. They are not a complete canonical V1 serving configuration. Do not combine them with --vllm-gr-config; use the canonical online example for the V1 service.

# default (xllm on NPU with xllm-ops installed; cascade otherwise)
vllm serve <model> --additional-config '{"vllm_gr_attention_backend": "CUSTOM"}'

# explicit xllm fused decode (fails fast at startup when xllm-ops is missing)
vllm serve <model> --additional-config '{"vllm_gr_attention_backend": "CUSTOM", "vllm_gr_npu_decode_execution": "xllm"}'

# explicit cascade (opt out of the fused path)
vllm serve <model> --additional-config '{"vllm_gr_attention_backend": "CUSTOM", "vllm_gr_npu_decode_execution": "cascade"}'

Notes:

  • The option is NPU-only; selecting xllm on a CUDA host raises at startup.
  • Mixed std/beam batches and mixed sliding-window / sink / ALiBI configs are not supported by the fused path; the scheduler falls back to the cascade operators for those cases, and unsorted or shrunk beam selections always reorder through the cascade kernel (the fused select_unshared_kv only encodes full-width parents grouped by source beam).

docs.title: Optional BSND Prefill graphs
docs.text: For full prompts without cached history, the opt-in BSND Prefill graph path avoids per-layer FIA parameter updates. It is disabled by default and requires no import overlay.
