docs.title: Serving and batching
docs.text: Start with Online serving and its successful single-prompt request. This page extends that setup to one four-prompt completions request, with fixed Beam width 128 and three generated SID components. Use the same installed accelerator environment, model snapshot, artifact, and repository root.

docs.title: A prompt list is different from concurrent requests
docs.text:
Workload HTTP requests Possible V1 execution One prompt 1 One single-item session Four prompts in one supported list 1 One session with four fixed members Four independent simultaneous calls 4 Separate sessions awaiting the execution owner

The V1 execution contract has one active execution owner and two dispatch slots. Those slots allow stages of that owner to overlap; they do not create two independent active sessions. Members of a batch are fixed before execution. This is not continuous batching or automatic coalescing across HTTP requests.

beam.online_batch_sizes selects exact prompt-list sizes that the completions route can submit as one session. The schema accepts unique integers in 1..8, requires 1, and normalizes their order. The default is [1, 2, 4]; the initial online guide deliberately uses [1]. Engine capacity, this HTTP policy, and graph captures are separate settings.

The route claims non-streaming Beam completions with ordinary text or token-ID prompts and a selected size. Other cases retain the original route. A list of three does not become batches of two and one under policy [1, 4]. Declines log Beam batch declined with the reason; they need not be HTTP errors.

docs.title: Size the whole execution
docs.text:
For fixed B=4 and width W=128, Decode has B * W = 512 physical token rows. max_num_seqs bounds logical requests: this batch needs at least 4, not 512. The physical Decode rows instead require a max_num_batched_tokens budget of at least 512 on NPU. Admission checks these two capacities separately. The launch command below retains --max-num-seqs 512 as generous headroom, not the minimum for B=4; larger settings can increase startup/resource costs. Neither capacity grants additional active execution owners.

Prefill has a different budget: sum all four complete input lengths, including the BEGIN token appended to each prompt. Chunked Prefill remains disabled. A 512-token Decode budget is insufficient for four 400-token prompts:

Decode rows:           4 * 128       = 512
Prefill input tokens:  4 * (400 + 1) = 1604

Use max_num_batched_tokens >= max(512, total_prepared_prompt_tokens) and allow for any smaller max_num_scheduled_tokens limit. Each prompt plus its effective generation budget must also fit max_model_len. The command below uses model length 512 and total token budget 2048; it is not a sizing rule for longer inputs. KV memory, model restrictions, and admission checks still apply.

docs.title: Prepare a four-prompt configuration
docs.text:
Stop the previous server before replacing it. In its accelerator shell, retain MODEL, BACKEND, and WORKDIR from the online or data-preparation guide. For a new shell, restore the actual values, for example:

export MODEL="$PWD/models/OneRec-1.7B"
export WORKDIR="$PWD/results/data-preparation"
export BACKEND=npu  # Use cuda for the CUDA installation.
export API=http://127.0.0.1:8000
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
test -f "$WORKDIR/vllm_gr_config.yaml"

If you prepared files under results/online-serving, restore that WORKDIR instead. Write a separate YAML while preserving the artifact identity:

python - <<'PY'
import os
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
from vllm_gr.config import gr_config_to_mapping, load_gr_config, gr_config_from_mapping

work = Path(os.environ["WORKDIR"]).resolve()
config = load_gr_config(work / "vllm_gr_config.yaml")
table = config.constraint_table
if table is None or not table.enabled or table.backend.value != os.environ["BACKEND"]:
    raise ValueError("Reuse an enabled table for the selected backend")
if config.beam_max_width != 128 or config.beam_max_decode_steps != 3:
    raise ValueError("This example requires capacity 128 and three SID steps")
raw = gr_config_to_mapping(config)
raw["beam"].update(online_batch_sizes=[1, 4], graph_batch_size=4)
gr_config_from_mapping(raw)
path = work / "vllm_gr_batch4.yaml"
path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(raw, sort_keys=False), encoding="utf-8")
print(path)
PY

The artifact remains shared configuration, not request data. All members use one Beam parameter set and one effective generation budget. Different prompt lengths are allowed if all budgets and model limits fit; the route does not silently shorten one request to match another. This example keeps the guide's CUDA graph setting and NPU eager setting.

Start the replacement server in the foreground:

device_args=()
if [ "$BACKEND" = npu ]; then
  device_args=(--block-size 128 --enforce-eager)
elif [ "$BACKEND" != cuda ]; then
  echo 'BACKEND must be cuda or npu' >&2
  exit 1
fi
vllm-gr serve "$MODEL" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --served-model-name onerec --trust-remote-code \
  --vllm-gr-config "$WORKDIR/vllm_gr_batch4.yaml" \
  --max-model-len 512 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 --max-logprobs 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
  --async-scheduling --no-enable-chunked-prefill \
  "${device_args[@]}"

This keeps TP/PP/DP/DCP/PCP at 1. The current V1 runtime requires a uniform text decoder, FP16/BF16, and no LoRA, quantization, speculative decoding, multimodal inputs, or KV transfer. Raising batch capacity does not add those capabilities.

docs.title: Check readiness and send one request
docs.text:
In a second terminal on the same host, activate the matching environment and restore MODEL and WORKDIR above, then run:

export API=http://127.0.0.1:8000
curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 5 "$API/health"
curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 5 "$API/v1/models" | python -m json.tool

Wait for HTTP 200 and the alias onerec. These checks establish service/engine availability, not that a B=4 request or its graph will succeed. Use the request below as the functional readiness check for this shape.

Generate valid JSON with four token-ID prompts. This makes the input IDs explicit and lets the response checker attribute choices even when fewer than 128 candidates survive. The same endpoint also accepts a list of text prompts.

python - <<'PY'
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(os.environ["MODEL"], trust_remote_code=True)
texts = [
    f"User {i}. Video history: <|sid_begin|><s_a_346><s_b_6566><s_c_5603><|sid_end|>.\n"
    "Recommend the next video."
    for i in range(4)
]
prompts = [tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False) for text in texts]
if any(not ids or len(ids) + 5 > 512 for ids in prompts):
    raise ValueError("Each input must fit the conservative public token budget")
if len({tuple(ids) for ids in prompts}) != 4:
    raise ValueError("Use four distinct prompts for this response-attribution example")
if sum(len(ids) + 1 for ids in prompts) > 2048:
    raise ValueError("Combined Prefill exceeds the server's token budget")
request = {
    "model": "onerec", "prompt": prompts,
    "use_beam_search": True, "stream": False,
    "n": 128, "temperature": 0.0, "max_tokens": 5,
    "ignore_eos": True, "skip_special_tokens": False,
    "include_stop_str_in_output": True, "return_token_ids": True,
    "vllm_xargs": {"begin_token": "<|sid_begin|>", "end_token": "<|sid_end|>"},
}
path = Path(os.environ["WORKDIR"]) / "batch4-request.json"
path.write_text(json.dumps(request, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
print("prepared_prefill_tokens=", sum(len(ids) + 1 for ids in prompts))
print(path)
PY

curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 120 \
  "$API/v1/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary "@$WORKDIR/batch4-request.json" \
  --output "$WORKDIR/batch4-response.json" \
  --write-out 'HTTP batch elapsed: %{time_total}s\n'

n is the per-prompt Beam width, not batch size. max_tokens=5 reserves the two markers and searches three SID components. The online V1 entry enforces ignore_eos=True. return_token_ids requests output IDs and accepted prompt IDs; this example does not request per-token log probabilities or chat templates. Constraint artifact paths and digests belong to server YAML, not this payload. See parameters for dynamic widths and platform limits. A prompt list does not enable NPU per_parent_beam_widths or per-prompt Multi-Trie selection in this snapshot. Those candidate/constraint capabilities must be checked separately from the number of prompts.

docs.title: Interpret choices and actual batching
docs.text:
The non-streaming response flattens prompt-major outputs and numbers index continuously. When every prompt returns 128 results, divmod(index, 128) gives the input position and rank. If fewer results survive, that shortcut is wrong. Use the requested prompt IDs for this example instead:

python - <<'PY'
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

work = Path(os.environ["WORKDIR"])
request = json.loads((work / "batch4-request.json").read_text())
response = json.loads((work / "batch4-response.json").read_text())
if "error" in response:
    raise SystemExit(response["error"])
owners = {tuple(ids): i for i, ids in enumerate(request["prompt"])}
counts = [0] * 4
for choice in response["choices"]:
    owner = owners[tuple(choice["prompt_token_ids"])]
    rank = counts[owner]
    counts[owner] += 1
    if rank == 0:
        print(owner, choice["index"], choice["token_ids"], choice["finish_reason"])
print("returned_per_prompt=", counts)
print("usage=", response.get("usage"))
PY

usage.prompt_tokens sums accepted original inputs; completion accounting sums the returned tails, including configured output boundaries. A legal SID does not establish recommendation quality. Compare quality for the deployed batch shape; B=1 and B=4 are not guaranteed to have identical numerical rankings.

The response shape alone cannot establish one B=4 session. Check server logs for Beam batch session ... prompts=4 and any Beam batch declined reason. Resource shortages can queue or reject work even after frontend checks pass.

docs.title: NPU graphs, timing, and shutdown
docs.text:
NPU Beam FULL replay needs the exact captured (logical batch, input width): (4, 128) differs from both (1, 128) and another factorization of 512 rows. To try it, enable beam.graph_enabled, retain graph_batch_size: 4, remove --enforce-eager, and restart. Dynamic schedules also need matching Decode input-width captures. Prefill capture has separate controls. CUDA ModelRunner V1 uses its own startup capture policy; this YAML does not guarantee B=4 replay.

NPU capture also requires the supported pure Beam/xllm path, persistent buffers, and request-ordered contiguous pool slots starting at 0. Pool slots identify members' KV storage, not independent execution owners. Internal _beam_graph_full_dispatch_count counts FULL dispatch selections; _beam_graph_fallback_count and its reason map count misses, not necessarily whole-forward eager execution. These are Worker diagnostics, not public HTTP fields. Use the validation guide for actual evidence.

The curl time includes queueing, HTTP, preprocessing, execution, and response construction for the whole list. Dividing by four does not measure an individual request's latency. For repeated steady-state runs, report batch latency and prompt throughput separately, with warmup, graph/cache state, and inputs fixed.

A client timeout closes its wait; it does not prove device work has drained. The claimed list route closes its generator on cancellation, and the async session client retains abort/release cleanup ownership. Do not assume every network disconnect, delegated route, or immediate retry has completed cleanup. Record the error and server logs before retrying instead of launching duplicate work automatically. To stop the foreground server you started, press Ctrl+C in that terminal and wait for shutdown. Avoid killing unrelated accelerator jobs.

Pinned sources: HTTP batch routing, admission, async cleanup, NPU graph gates, and vLLM 0.30 response flattening.

docs.title: Testing and CI
docs.text: Select validation from the behavior being changed, using the installed runtime for that platform. Read Developer guide for code ownership and Validation and benchmarking for comparing inference results. Commands below belong to the inference repository root.

docs.title: Choose the right evidence
docs.text:
Level What it establishes Main prerequisites Documentation checks Formatting, characters, spelling, links, and command consistency Selected hooks; no accelerator Host/contract regression Configuration, routing, ownership, or isolated function behavior The test's actual dependencies and fixtures Kernel/integration tests Numerical and layout behavior of selected device paths Matching CUDA or Ascend runtime and allocated device Model/system tests End-to-end public API, lifecycle, numerical output, or graph behavior Model snapshot, artifact, runtime, device, and test data Benchmark acceptance Results against the resolved accuracy/performance policy Fixed dataset, input identity, baseline, and saved evidence Wheel smoke Installation metadata and import behavior outside the checkout Build tools and packaging dependencies

A host-oriented test can require Torch and vLLM through tests/conftest.py, even when it never accesses a device. A CPU wheel or reference selector does not establish a production CPU Beam inference runtime. Inspect collection, fixtures, availability guards, and model requirements before choosing a command.

Each test needs its registered tier: cpu_test, gpu_test, or npu_test. model_test is an additional requirement, not a replacement for a platform tier. Missing tier declarations can fail collection. Markers do not themselves skip tests; selection expressions and availability guards have separate roles. Follow the test-tier rules for mixed modules instead of using a broad not cpu_test filter that drops device cases within CPU modules.

docs.title: Start with targeted checks
docs.text:
For a configuration change, inspect and run the owning regression file:

python -m pytest -q tests/test_gr_config_v1.py

For selected kernel/integration behavior, use the respective prepared runtime and replace device 0 with the device allocated to your run:

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/test_rec_constrained_topk_cuda.py
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest -q tests/constraints/test_npu_backend_integration.py

For OneRec-1.7B system coverage, set VLLM_GR_TEST_MODEL to the local directory containing configuration, tokenizer, and weights. For example, in Ascend:

VLLM_GR_TEST_MODEL=/absolute/path/to/OneRec-1.7B \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
python -m pytest --run-slow -q tests/st/test_onerec_v1_npu_e2e.py

That suite needs the Ascend stack and xllm Beam operators. Its own shape/bucket contract determines coverage; success is not evidence for every padding shape. CUDA's corresponding scheduling entry is tests/st/test_onerec_v1_scheduler_st.py. Missing prerequisites can cause skips or failures. HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 prevents model-hub fallback downloads, not every possible setup operation. Report the actual selected/passed/skipped cases.

docs.title: Check documentation without launching the full suite
docs.text:
Use explicit hook IDs on the complete changed file list. Replace the example path below with the real Markdown paths:

pre-commit run markdownlint --files docs/development.md
pre-commit run check-characters --files docs/development.md
pre-commit run typos --files docs/development.md
pre-commit run end-of-file-fixer --files docs/development.md
pre-commit run trailing-whitespace --files docs/development.md
pre-commit run mixed-line-ending --files docs/development.md
git diff --check

Also inspect new untracked files, relative links, commands, and generated-site navigation. A strict site build is useful when changing site configuration; Markdown lint alone does not establish that a command works or a page resolves.

pre-commit run --all-files includes the full slow pytest suite. Even pre-commit run --files ... can invoke the run-tests hook, whose pass_filenames: false does not narrow pytest to those files. Do not substitute either command for the documentation-only hooks above.

docs.title: Understand inference-repository CI
docs.text:
For PRs into main or decode_graph, full validation requires a non-draft PR and the ready label. Pushing while it remains, adding it, or marking a labeled draft ready can start validation. Removing it or converting to draft cancels the old PR run and skips new validation. Wheel builds have their own path filters.

abtest requests a separate performance A/B path for eligible non-draft PRs; its success alone does not satisfy the full gate. Confirmed documentation-only PRs do not run A/B, even with that label. Other label changes are not a general request to run full CI. Review events can also trigger this workflow; a newer run can cancel the previous run for the same PR. Inspect the current head.

The narrow docs-only classifier covers Markdown under docs/ and designated root Markdown files (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md). It still requires the applicable non-draft/label conditions. Site YAML, SVG, requirements, mixed changes, or uncertain classification are not automatically eligible just because their purpose is documentation. The target branch must already contain the classifier; independent Jenkins jobs have separate rules.

The required Benchmark blocking gate checks the relevant documentation/full jobs and rejects failed, cancelled, or skipped blocking results. A queued job has no passing result yet; inspect runner assignment and logs before blaming the change. See Contributing and the pinned workflow.

docs.title: Preserve accuracy and performance boundaries
docs.text:
Legal SIDs and passing device tests do not establish Recall. Compare tokens, scores, rankings, and model/dataset metrics according to the declared contract. Graph flags are not replay evidence, and an eager/graph comparison is different from a cross-version performance comparison. Keep numerical and latency results separate, with identical inputs and recorded graph/cache/warmup settings.

Acceptance policy is resolved by target branch, device, and baseline provenance. Do not relax thresholds, replace failures with skips, or select a new dataset to make a gate pass. Record code/import origin, runtime, device, model/tokenizer, artifact, command, baseline/candidate identity, and output files. Historical measurements only support their recorded configuration; a Jenkins success does not automatically update GitHub Actions or validate a different PR revision.

These CI rules belong to the inference repository. The separate website publication repository has its own deployment checks and permissions; publishing generated pages neither runs accelerator CI nor grants access to their source.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the first specific error in the engine or Worker log. A final Engine core initialization failed message usually summarizes an earlier failure. Keep the model, inputs, and command unchanged while isolating one cause. Use Quickstart for the supported first-run configuration.

docs.title: Files are missing or tee cannot create a log
docs.text:
Symptom Check Action FileNotFoundError for a relative catalog or prompt path The shell's current directory Run the examples from the vllm-gr source repository root. Model directory is missing or incomplete Local weights, config.json, and tokenizer files Download the model separately; the repository does not contain its weights. tee: ... No such file or directory The log's parent directory Create that directory before running the pipeline. Variables work in one terminal but not another Variables in the active shell Set the paths again in the new terminal, as the online guide does.

After setting the paths in First offline inference:

pwd
test -f "$MODEL/config.json"
test -f "$CATALOG"
test -f "$PROMPT"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR/logs"
set -o pipefail

pipefail makes an inference failure visible when output is piped through tee. It does not create directories or repair an invalid path.

docs.title: Python imports the wrong checkout or runtime
docs.text:
Check the interpreter and the actual package location in the shell that starts the engine:

python --version
python -m pip --version
python -c 'import sys, vllm_gr; print(sys.executable); print(vllm_gr.__file__)'

If the import path points to an unexpected environment or checkout, activate the intended environment and install this checkout using its platform guide. Use python -m pip to target that interpreter. Installing GR does not provision or upgrade the Ascend vendor stack. Installing into one Python environment does not repair another environment.

Run vllm-gr check-env for CUDA or vllm-gr check-env --npu for Ascend. These checks establish runtime compatibility, not successful model inference, operator execution, or sufficient device memory.

docs.title: Ascend dependencies or custom operators fail to load
docs.text:
The source version behind these guides requires vLLM 0.30.0, vLLM-Ascend 0.30.0rc2, and Triton-Ascend 3.6.0 from the prepared vendor environment. Follow Ascend installation; an environment named after an older release does not become compatible just by installing GR.

Symptom Check Action Unsupported vLLM or vLLM-Ascend version The active interpreter's package versions Return to the matching vendor image instead of mixing release stacks. Triton-Ascend is installed but its backend is missing The active triton module, reported by check-env --npu Resolve the shared-package overwrite described by the error; standard Triton metadata alone is insufficient. custom_ops_lib cannot be imported or a shared library is missing CANN, the installed custom operator environment, and the active Python Load the CANN and custom xllm-ops environments from the installation guide in this shell. A required binding is missing The installed xllm-ops build and exported callables Build the required operator subset for this image's CANN version and reinstall its Python binding.

The Python binding is named custom_ops_lib. custom_xllm_math is the CANN vendor directory, not the Python module name. On the prepared NPU host, this checks binding exposure without launching an inference request:

python - <<'PY'
from vllm_gr.ops.npu._xllm_loader import custom_ops

ops = custom_ops()
if ops is None:
    raise SystemExit("custom_ops_lib is unavailable; check the installed runtime and loader logs")

names = (
    "cache_unshared_kv", "x_attention", "select_unshared_kv",
    "beam_search_group", "beam_search_rec_final_select", "rec_constrained_topk",
)
for name in names:
    print(name, callable(getattr(ops, name, None)))
PY

Successful import and callable checks do not establish ABI compatibility or successful execution on the device. Keep the original loader error if this fails. Do not reuse custom operators compiled for a different CANN stack. Attention's cascade fallback does not supply a missing catalog-constrained TopK operator: that resolver has no Torch fallback. See the binding loader and constrained TopK resolver.

Keep pip check reports as diagnostics. The vendor image has documented metadata discrepancies; distinguish those from a new missing dependency or a failed NumPy/cv2 import, as explained in the Ascend installation guide.

docs.title: Engine startup reports insufficient free memory
docs.text:
Read the reported free memory and requested utilization. The startup check can fail before inference when other jobs occupy the device. Check the allocated device with nvidia-smi or npu-smi info, according to your platform.

Use a free device through your environment's allocation process. Stop only your own unneeded inference jobs; do not terminate other users' processes. gpu_memory_utilization also applies on NPU. Lower it only when enough memory remains for weights, KV storage, and execution buffers; lowering it blindly can move the failure to a later allocation. Wider Beams and additional graph captures can require more memory. A memory-admission error alone is not a numerical-accuracy failure.

docs.title: An argument is unknown or configuration sources conflict
docs.text:
Configuration layer Put settings here GR engine configuration beam and constraint_table in --vllm-gr-config YAML or the Python vllm_gr_config mapping. Native engine configuration Supported GRLLM/serve options such as max_model_len, async_scheduling, and gpu_memory_utilization. Beam request Python BeamSearchParams, or HTTP fields and supported vllm_xargs entries. Platform extension Only keys and nesting supported by the installed vLLM-Ascend release's additional_config.

An EngineArgs.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument error means the argument was not accepted at that layer. Do not pass platform switches such as enable_npugraph_ex as arbitrary top-level GRLLM keywords. Check the exact vendor release's configuration contract before moving a setting elsewhere.

Do not combine canonical GR configuration with legacy GR catalog, attention, or Beam overrides in CLI options or additional_config. Restore the complete online example before adding custom settings. Keep async_scheduling=True, Chunked Prefill disabled, and request width equal to beam.max_width. HTTP n is this Beam width, not a display limit. See Beam parameters and modes and the configuration boundary.

docs.title: A graph does not replay, or fallback counts increase
docs.text:
On NPU, first confirm the eager example works. Then select graph execution without changing the inputs. For serving, enable beam.graph_enabled, remove --enforce-eager, and restart the engine. The offline demo's --execution option controls NPU; it does not switch CUDA into eager mode.

Inspect npu_beam_graph counters from the NPU graph example:

Observation Interpretation or action No Decode replay for one generated component Expected: this request finishes in Prefill. Missing (B, input_width) in captured_shapes Configure the exact logical batch size and Decode input widths before engine startup. Increasing fallbacks Inspect fallback_reasons; Beam FULL was not used, but execution need not be purely eager. More dispatches than measured Decode steps Counters include warmup as well as measured or profiled requests.

For retained widths [128, 64, 32], Decode inputs are 128 and 64, not 32. Capture only the needed shapes. Prefill capture has separate controls and precision limits. Configuration flags alone are not replay evidence; inspect the counters and a separate profile. See graph shape configuration.

docs.title: SID candidates, scores, or ranking differ
docs.text:
Compare the same model/tokenizer snapshot, catalog, prompt token IDs, dtype, batch size, generation budget, candidate domain, widths, and cache policy. The direct offline demo truncates or pads to --input-len; the HTTP example does not apply that preprocessing. Identical prompt text alone is insufficient.

Compare ordered sequences, candidate sets, and scores for matching sequences separately. A different Beam schedule or full-vocabulary versus SID-family normalization changes the search semantics. Catalog-free SID stages do not guarantee that a generated combination identifies a known item. Valid SIDs also do not establish unchanged recommendation quality.

For NPU, the recorded exact-bucket tests do not resolve the open padded-Prefill precision limitation. Do not claim arbitrary mixed-length Graph/Eager parity from a passing bounded case. Isolate Decode with Prefill graphs disabled when following the recorded reproducer, and preserve its input conditions. See Validation and benchmarking and the documented precision scope.

docs.title: HTTP requests or artifact validation fail
docs.text:
Symptom Check Action Connection refused Server startup, host, and port Keep the server running and use the address selected in the online guide. Model not found /v1/models and --served-model-name Send the configured alias, onerec in the guide. Artifact or tokenizer digest mismatch Artifact path, both digests, and tokenizer snapshot Rebuild the artifact and YAML together; do not edit a digest to bypass validation. Triples JSON supplied as a server catalog Artifact format Compile a persistent .safetensors table for the online service. Width or budget error Request n, server capacity, and boundary positions Keep width 128; max_tokens=5 with begin/end reserves three generated components.

Read the response error body and the first specific server error. A length finish reason can be normal for fixed-budget Beam; it is not automatically a failed generation. Follow Online serving for the complete request and artifact setup.

docs.title: Collect a small diagnostic record
docs.text:
Run these basic checks in the failing environment; they do not run inference:

python --version
git rev-parse HEAD
python -m pip --version
python - <<'PY'
from importlib import metadata, util

for name in ("vllm-gr", "vllm", "vllm-ascend", "torch", "torch-npu", "triton-ascend"):
    try:
        print(name, metadata.version(name))
    except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        print(name, "not installed")
for name in ("vllm_gr", "vllm", "torch", "triton"):
    spec = util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, "module:", None if spec is None else spec.origin)
PY

Record the selected device and runtime-check result, the first error and nearby context, the exact command, relevant graph settings, and whether eager works. For a numerical issue, include model/input identity and matching token/score evidence. For performance, include the timing boundary and repeated samples. Remove credentials, private paths, and private endpoint names before sharing. Do not dump the full environment, credential files, or authentication headers.

docs.title: Validation and benchmarking
docs.text:
After Quickstart, check correctness before measuring performance. A successful request, numerical agreement, recommendation quality, graph replay, and latency are different kinds of evidence.

This guide reuses the MODEL, CATALOG, and PROMPT paths from First offline inference. Run commands from the source repository root in the matching CUDA or Ascend environment, with an available device. Use an idle device and stop your other inference workloads before comparing timings.

docs.title: Decide what you are validating
docs.text:
Check What to inspect Functional execution The request completes, outputs have the expected structure, and constrained candidates follow the catalog. Graph execution Actual capture/replay and fallback evidence for the intended Prefill and Decode shapes. Numerical agreement Candidate token sequences, ordering, and scores under otherwise matching conditions. Recommendation quality Recall or other task metrics on an identified dataset with ground truth and matching item mappings. Performance Repeated measurements with fixed inputs, an explicit timing boundary, and saved run conditions.

Importing a package, collecting tests, or skipping unavailable tests does not establish inference correctness. Catalog-valid SIDs alone do not establish recommendation quality. A graph run does not by itself establish a speedup.

docs.title: Check numerical behavior
docs.text:
For a baseline/candidate or NPU eager/graph comparison, hold model weights, tokenizer, catalog, prompt token IDs and lengths, dtype, batch size, Beam width, candidate count, generation budget, return limit, and cache policy constant. Record runner and graph settings as part of each case.

Compare three things separately:

  1. The ordered list of returned token sequences.
  2. The set of candidates, to distinguish a ranking change from a changed search set.
  3. Scores for matching token sequences, rather than unrelated candidates at the same rank. Follow the owning test's numerical contract.

Changing a dynamic Beam schedule or a candidate probability domain changes the search semantics. Such a comparison measures a quality/performance tradeoff, rather than numerical parity under an identical search.

The development environment includes real-model system coverage. These commands load weights and run on the selected accelerator; they require pytest and the project's test dependencies as well as the inference runtime:

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
VLLM_GR_TEST_MODEL="$MODEL" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
python -m pytest --run-slow -q -rs \
  tests/st/test_onerec_v1_scheduler_st.py

VLLM_GR_TEST_MODEL="$MODEL" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
python -m pytest --run-slow -q -rs \
  tests/st/test_onerec_v1_npu_e2e.py

Inspect the test summary and skip reasons. Passing these cases covers their configured workloads; validate the batch sizes, widths, input lengths, and model used by your deployment separately.

NPU Prefill accuracy scope

The bounded NPU graph subtest uses width 8 and exact Prefill buckets. It is not a width-128 business-quality benchmark. The source also documents an open padded-Prefill precision limitation; passing the exact-bucket case does not establish numerical agreement for arbitrary mixed-length padded inputs. See the recorded scope and reproducer.

For task accuracy, use the established dataset and acceptance policy. The GPU five-task Recall gate and Video-100 gate used on NPU have different input and policy requirements. The GPU A100 calibration is not an absolute accuracy target for NPU. Read the preparation requirements before running a formal gate; do not change its thresholds to make a result pass.

docs.title: Measure offline API latency
docs.text:
Use a fresh output directory for each experiment. The following also creates the parent directories used by tee and preserves failures in piped commands:

export RUN_DIR="$PWD/results/beam-validation/$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/json" "$RUN_DIR/logs" "$RUN_DIR/profile"
set -o pipefail
git rev-parse HEAD > "$RUN_DIR/source-revision.txt"
sha256sum "$CATALOG" "$PROMPT" > "$RUN_DIR/input-sha256.txt"

Also record local source changes, the model snapshot, tokenizer/artifact identities, installed runtime versions, device, dtype, complete command, and graph environment settings. An unchanged path does not prove unchanged input contents. The benchmark JSON does not automatically record all of these details.

Choose the command for the runtime being measured. For an NPU eager/graph comparison, run those two commands separately with the same prepared inputs:

CUDA GPUNPU eagerNPU graph 
python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" --catalog "$CATALOG" --prompt "$PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend cuda --execution graph \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 \
  --input-len 128 --generated-steps 3 --print-beams 5 \
  --warmup-runs 3 --repeat 20 \
  --output-json "$RUN_DIR/json/cuda-graph.json" \
  2>&1 | tee "$RUN_DIR/logs/cuda-graph.log"

python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" --catalog "$CATALOG" --prompt "$PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend npu --execution eager \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 \
  --input-len 128 --generated-steps 3 --print-beams 5 \
  --warmup-runs 3 --repeat 20 \
  --output-json "$RUN_DIR/json/npu-eager.json" \
  2>&1 | tee "$RUN_DIR/logs/npu-eager.log"

python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" --catalog "$CATALOG" --prompt "$PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend npu --execution graph \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 \
  --input-len 128 --generated-steps 3 --print-beams 5 \
  --warmup-runs 3 --repeat 20 \
  --output-json "$RUN_DIR/json/npu-graph.json" \
  2>&1 | tee "$RUN_DIR/logs/npu-graph.log"

The CUDA command explicitly labels the report as graph; --execution still only controls the NPU runtime. It is not a CUDA eager/graph toggle.

docs.title: What the timer includes
docs.text:
The script runs three untimed warmup batches, then measures 20 complete beam_search_v1(..., output_mode="full") calls until output objects return. For this three-component example, each call includes Prefill and two Decode forwards, together with the API work needed to return the results.

Engine startup, artifact compilation, warmup, pre-call prompt preparation, and post-call result inspection/printing are outside the timing boundary. Prefix Cache remains enabled, but independent salts per row and run force cold Prefill; this is not a prefix-cache-hit benchmark.

This is batch API latency. It is neither device-kernel-only time nor HTTP latency. For larger batches, dividing batch P50 by batch size gives an amortized cost, not the latency experienced by each request.

docs.title: Read the benchmark JSON
docs.text:
The JSON file contains the report directly. Standard output wraps the same report under beam_benchmark. For example, after the NPU graph run:

python - "$RUN_DIR/json/npu-graph.json" <<'PY'
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

report = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
print(report["timing_scope"])
print("batch P50 (ms):", report["batch_latency_ms"]["p50"])
print("batch P95 (ms):", report["batch_latency_ms"]["p95"])
print("requests/s:", report["requests_per_second"])
print("returned beams/s:", report["returned_beams_per_second"])
PY
Field Meaning batch_latency_ms Mean, P50, P95, minimum, and maximum batch API latency, in milliseconds. requests_per_second Timed request count divided by total timed seconds. returned_beams_per_second Actual returned candidate count divided by total timed seconds. runs[].returned_beams Actual total returned candidates across the whole batch in that run. npu_beam_graph Capture, replay, and fallback diagnostics for NPU graph runs.

The benchmark file does not serialize all candidate token IDs and scores. Only the final batch's leading results are printed, limited by --print-beams. Use a dedicated correctness run to capture complete results for numerical comparison; the timing JSON alone is not precision evidence.

Twenty samples form a short local measurement. Repeat controlled experiments and inspect run-to-run variation before claiming a regression or improvement. Changing the search width or return limit also changes the workload, so record it when comparing throughput.

docs.title: Collect a separate profile
docs.text:
Use the same inputs and workload, but collect traces in a separate process:

CUDA GPUAscend NPU 
python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" --catalog "$CATALOG" --prompt "$PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend cuda --execution graph \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 \
  --input-len 128 --generated-steps 3 --print-beams 5 \
  --profile-dir "$RUN_DIR/profile/cuda-graph" \
  --profile-warmup-runs 1 --profile-runs 5 \
  2>&1 | tee "$RUN_DIR/logs/cuda-graph-profile.log"

python -u examples/offline_inference/beam_search/offline_beam_search_v1.py \
  --model "$MODEL" --catalog "$CATALOG" --prompt "$PROMPT" \
  --constraint-backend npu --execution graph \
  --batch-size 1 --beam-width 128 \
  --input-len 128 --generated-steps 3 --print-beams 5 \
  --profile-dir "$RUN_DIR/profile/npu-graph" \
  --profile-warmup-runs 1 --profile-runs 5 \
  2>&1 | tee "$RUN_DIR/logs/npu-graph-profile.log"

The profiler starts after engine initialization and one unprofiled warmup, then collects five complete batches before output printing. It records the Worker side with stack, shape, and memory recording disabled. Inspect the supplied directory and its worker/rank subdirectories for traces.

Do not combine --repeat with --profile-dir. In direct Beam mode, --output-json requires --repeat, so leave it out of profiling commands too. Do not layer this collection with msprof or use profiled samples as the unprofiled latency result.

Profiles help locate TensorMove, TopK, attention, and other operator costs. Fewer operators or lower copy time is a hypothesis for an improvement; confirm the effect with separate API latency measurements.

docs.title: Verify graph evidence and record the conclusion
docs.text:
For NPU graph runs, inspect captured_shapes, full_dispatches, fallbacks, and fallback_reasons under npu_beam_graph. Counters include warmup as well as collected or timed runs, so do not expect only the measured Decode count. A one-step run ends in Prefill without Decode replay. A fallback does not necessarily mean a purely eager forward.

Keep the evidence separate in your report: functional result, numerical or quality comparison, observed graph shapes, timing scope, measured latency distribution, and relevant profiles. Use the same saved conditions when checking a code change in a fresh process.

Formal CI acceptance has additional input and policy checks. See the validation levels and benchmark acceptance guide before using the CI-oriented runners. Local demo measurements do not replace those gates.

If a run fails or graph execution differs from the intended mode, start with Troubleshooting and keep the first underlying error with your validation record.
